<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>



</system-reminder>

# Planning notes for mission artifacts (orchestrator, 2026-10-22)

Read this before any other mission file. It records what the owner decided after `SPEC.md` v0.2 was
written, and the readiness facts the mission is built on. Where these notes and `SPEC.md` disagree,
these notes win (owner decisions after the spec); `SPEC.md` is amended as-built at the next
integration (RULES rule 8). Where these notes are silent, `SPEC.md` is the authority.

Repository: `/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory`).
Mission branch: `mission/observatory-v1` (created from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`).
Owner: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`).

## Files to read for context (all in the repository)

- `SPEC.md` (v0.2): §2 mission setup, §3 milestones S, M0–M5 with named tests and acceptance
  commands, §4 versions, §5 architecture, §6 tests, §7 CI, §8 deliverables.
- `ai/RULES.md` (binding), `AGENTS.md` (operational summary), `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6
  (FR ids, lanes, §7 event kinds, §10 metrics, appendix A canonical event).
- `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md` and
  `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md` (measured facts, pasted numbers).
- `config/observatory.example.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
  `docs/decisions/*.md`.

## Owner decisions after SPEC v0.1 (2026-10-22), all binding

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is
   selected from the Droid version recorded in the **fixture header** (`droid --version`, 0.247.0
   at capture). Token usage, model, tags and child linkage are read from the sibling
   `<session-id>.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`,
   `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage`, `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`,
   `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`). Child sessions are sibling files linked by
   `session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`. JSONL `type` values seen: `message`,
   `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`, `session_start`; `modelId`,
   `apiProvider`, `reasoningEffort` sit on assistant messages. Decision file at S integration; SPEC
   §3 M0 / §5.2 amended as-built then.
2. **Keyring.** `keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 (feature `keychain`,
   `set_default_store`) instead of `keyring` 4.x (fails `cargo deny`). Keychain items are generic
   passwords with service `droid-observatory/<name>` and account = the login user (`dct`), not the

1→# droid-observatory — Spec for the mission
2→
3→Owner: David Carbajosa (architect, reviewer, the human in lane 7). Implementers: one Factory
4→Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) under ai/RULES.md. Status: v0.1 approved by the owner
5→(2026-10-22); v0.2: §5.8 concurrency limits added (owner decision 2026-10-22). Living document: §9 is the human feedback channel, §10 the as-built history.
6→
7→Inputs: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` (v0.5), `ai/prd/review-2026-10-22.md`, `ai/RULES.md`,
8→`ai/SPEC-TEMPLATE.md`, `docs/decisions/D-001..D-010`, `BACKLOG.md`, `config/observatory.example.toml`,
9→`config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` entries 17–21.
10→
11→Approval boundary: this document is the contract the mission plans from. Until the owner answers
12→`approved`, nothing else happens: no milestone plan, no worktree, no application code, no GitHub
13→object. After approval the mission plans from this file only (rule 9: deviations are proposed with
14→reason and cost, and wait).
15→
16→## 1. Purpose
17→
18→**What it is.** A Rust desktop application (Tauri 2 shell, Leptos UI, `observatory-core` library)
19→that shows one Factory Mission moving through nine lanes (PRD §7): Intent, Orchestrator, Workers,
20→Validators-scrutiny, Validators-user-testing, Integration, Human, Outside, and Time/Waste/Cost/models.
21→Cards are milestones with their features inside (PRD §8); every lane entry is a view over the raw
22→JSONL line it came from, never a copy (PRD §11.2).
23→
24→**For whom.** The mission owner who runs missions from a terminal and wants to see flow and cost;
25→the reviewer who opens Details and merges; the engineering lead who compares models over time
26→(PRD §6). Single user, local data, the user's own GitHub access.
27→
28→**What it must prove.** The mission is done when all of these hold on the mission branch:
29→
30→1. **Attach.** A mission started from any terminal on this machine appears on the board and every
31→   event of it shows within 1 s (FR-L1, FR-B6), with no control channel.
32→2. **Replay with a frozen mapping.** `observatory-cli replay` over the frozen capture ends with
33→   `unknown events: 0`, and the board renders the same capture with correct lane positions
34→   (FR-L2, FR-B7, rule 18).
35→3. **Host.** A mission launched from the app shows events within 1 s and the pause, message and
36→   answer controls reach the orchestrator (FR-L3, FR-H1..H4).
37→4. **Gate and fix loop.** Against the demo branch pair in this repository (§3 M4): a red check
38→   opens a `fix` cycle on the affected card, a green check with a human policy shows Merge, and
39→   merging from the app flips the badge (FR-G3..G8).
40→5. **Time, waste, cost.** Metrics recomputed from the frozen capture match the owner's reference
41→   spreadsheet within rounding (FR-M1..M7, PRD §10); every cost names its price-table date.
42→6. **The build is the first dataset.** The sessions of this mission are the capture that M0
43→   freezes and M5 is measured against (rule 17).
44→
45→**Out of scope (explicit).** PRD §5 non-goals: planning inside the app, multi-user or server
46→deployment, writing to Factory's hosted API beyond what `droid` does, editing or reviewing code in
47→the app, CI systems other than GitHub Actions. Also out: CI telemetry to Grafana (B-002), a
48→dedicated error tracker (B-003), Linux and Windows bundles (macOS is the target; the devcontainer
49→is core-only, B-001), the app performing any merge other than the human-confirmed Merge button
50→(FR-G5): v1 never merges on its own. Observing a merge performed by a ruleset or a bot stays in
51→scope: the gate badge shows `policy-merged` on detection (FR-G6, M4). Also out: a second mapping
52→version for Droid releases newer than the one captured. Guard: the mapper is versioned from day
53→one, every `Event` carries `mapping_version`, and the unknown-event count is always visible (tray,
54→CLI summary, exported series), so the first Droid upgrade shows as a rising count, never as a
55→silently broken board. And out: migrating the backlog before the mission starts (entry 19).
56→
57→**What this spec answers.** The review note `ai/prd/review-2026-10-22.md` item 5 (attach is the
58→primary live mode, D-008). The owner decisions logged after PRD v0.5: the telemetry contract and
59→series budget (D-010, B-017, §5.7), M4 on a demo branch pair in this repository instead of a
60→private demo repository (entry 19, B-007, §3 M4), the hybrid backlog driven by the mission
61→(entry 19, §8), the orchestrator model id `claude-fable-5.1` (entry 21, D-006 correction, §2),
62→and the backlog items the spec session owns: B-005 (§6), B-010 (§3), B-014 (§7), B-017 (§5.7).
63→
64→## 2. Mission setup
65→
66→**Command** (run by the owner from the repository root on a checkout of `main` that contains this
67→approved spec; the mission creates `mission/observatory-v1` from it):
68→
69→```sh
70→droid exec --mission --auto high \
71→  --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
72→  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort high \
73→  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
74→  --output-format text \
75→  -f SPEC.md
76→```
77→
78→| Flag | Value | Reason |
79→|---|---|---|
80→| `--mission --auto high` | required | Missions auto-approve proposals and need `--auto high` (Droid 0.247.0 `droid exec --help`). The hooks in `.factory/hooks.json` are the guard, not the prompt. |
81→| `--model` | `claude-fable-5.1` | Orchestrator (D-006, corrected 2026-10-22 from the misspelt `claude-fable-5-1`, which fell back to GPT-6 Sol). Factory catalog id, 4× multiplier. |
82→| `--reasoning-effort` | `high` | Fable's default; planning and integration are where judgment is bought. `xhigh`/`max` on a 4× model is not justified before a measured need. |
83→| `--worker-model` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Workers (D-006). 0.8× multiplier. Catalog id per docs.factory.com/models; `droid exec --help` on this machine lists `claude-sonnet-5` but not `claude-sonnet-5-5`; owner confirmed available on 2026-10-22. |
84→| `--worker-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Owner decision 2026-10-22: the model default; Rust compile errors and Leptos (little training data, PRD §12) need the reasoning. The cost/quality split lane 9 measures is between models, not efforts. |
85→| `--validator-model` | `claude-opus-5-5` | Validators, scrutiny and user testing (D-006). 1.6× multiplier. |
86→| `--validator-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Above Opus's default `medium`: validation is where correctness is bought (D-006 alternatives). |
87→| `--output-format` | `text` | The terminal is for the human; the dataset is the session JSONL under `~/.factory/sessions/`, which attach and replay read. |
88→| `-f SPEC.md` | this file | The mission plans from the approved spec (template, last paragraph). |
89→
90→The same values are declared in `.factory/settings.json` so that a mission started from the
91→Factory App uses them: `missionOrchestratorModel`, `missionOrchestratorReasoningEffort`,
92→`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `.workerReasoningEffort`, `.validationWorkerModel`,
93→`.validationWorkerReasoningEffort`. The three reasoning-effort keys are added with the spec PR
94→(§8). A change to any model is a decision file (rule 19).
95→
96→**Mission branch.** `mission/observatory-v1`, created from `main` at the commit that contains this
97→approved spec. One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end of the mission, opened
98→by the orchestrator, merged by the human after `gate` is green. Nothing else reaches `main`
99→(rule 12). The branch is deleted at the merge (PRD §2).
100→
101→**Worktree policy.** One worktree per milestone: `git worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m>
102→mission/observatory-v1` where `<m>` is `s`, `m0` … `m5`. Workers and validators of a milestone
103→work only inside its worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13); the shared files
104→(`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) are written by
105→the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration. Integration is `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`
106→into `mission/observatory-v1` by the orchestrator, then `make check` locally, then the
107→`mission-checks` run on the push must be green before the next milestone starts. A worktree is
108→removed after integration; its branch stays (history).
109→
110→**Gate command.** `make check` is the only local gate: it is exactly what `mission-branch.yml`
111→runs (rule 5). A worker hands off only with `make check` green in its worktree; the orchestrator
112→integrates only with `make check` green on the mission branch.
113→
114→**Hooks that must be active.** `.factory/hooks.json`: `guard-git.sh` (PreToolUse on `Execute`,
115→blocks amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push/push-to-main) and `log-tool-call.sh` (PostToolUse,
116→appends one JSON line per tool call to `build-log/<UTC-day>/<session>.jsonl`). Git hooks via
117→`make hooks` (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`): `pre-commit` (gitleaks on staged files, file size, debt
118→markers, decisions index, rustfmt, markdownlint), `commit-msg` (subject ≤ 72 chars, no WIP/fixup),
119→`pre-push` (no `main`, no non-fast-forward). A worker that finds a hook missing stops and reports;
120→it never disables or bypasses one (`--no-verify` is a rule 12 violation).
121→
122→**Usage budget per milestone.** Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed
123→from the token counts Factory reports for the mission's sessions (the usage page or the stream's
124→`usage.reported`), pasted into `reports/usage/<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 7). Factory
125→Standard Credits are recorded next to it when visible. The caps below are the owner's planning
126→numbers, not measurements; this is the first mission and there is no prior run to calibrate on.
127→At the M0 boundary the orchestrator proposes re-caps for M1–M5 from the measured S and M0 usage
128→(owner decision 2026-10-22); until then the table stands.
129→
130→| Milestone | Cap (USD-eq) | Reason for the size |
131→|---|---|---|
132→| S  walking skeleton | 40 | Thin slice, few files, mostly scaffolding and one fixture. |
133→| M0 capture and mapping | 60 | Mapper plus golden tests; the capture already exists (§3 M0). |
134→| M1 board, replay, attach | 150 | Largest UI milestone and the Leptos go/no-go; rework budget inside. |
135→| M2 host | 80 | RPC adapter plus launch screen; the control channel is new ground. |
136→| M3 intervention | 60 | Lane-7 semantics over M2 controls; small surface. |
137→| M4 branch, gate, fix loop | 120 | Two adapters (git, GitHub), the demo branch pair, a live PR loop. |
138→| M5 time, waste, cost | 120 | The metric engine and its oracle test; export; charts. |
139→| Total | 630 | Hard stop for the mission; the final PR and fixes come out of the unspent remainder. |
140→
141→At a cap the orchestrator stops dispatching, writes the usage so far to `reports/usage/`, raises
142→the stall flag and waits for the human (rule 15). Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9).
143→
144→**What the human will answer mid-mission.** Only at a milestone boundary or when the stall flag is
145→up (rule 15): the M1 go/no-go (PRD §12), a budget cap reached, a proposed deviation from this spec
146→with its reason and cost, a keychain item or GitHub permission the mission cannot create itself
147→(§3 M4, §5.9), the reference spreadsheet for M5 (B-008), and a red `gate` on the final PR.
148→
149→**What the human will not answer.** Style, naming, crate choice within §4, test structure, how to
150→split a milestone into features, which worker does what, or anything already decided here or in

386→## 5. Architecture
387→
388→Each decision carries its reason. Numbers come from the PRD and `config/observatory.example.toml`
389→unless a reason says otherwise.
390→
391→### 5.1 Crates and interfaces
392→
393→| Crate / app | Responsibility | Public interface | Reason |
394→|---|---|---|---|
395→| `crates/observatory-core` | ingest, model, mapping, store, metrics, control, telemetry; **no UI dependency, sync, no tokio** | `Source` trait, `Event`, `Store`, `Metrics`, `Control`, `Config` | Testable from fixtures alone; every milestone's logic lives here so the UI can be swapped (PRD §12 go/no-go). |
396→| `crates/observatory-cli` | headless `replay`, `inspect`, `attach --watch`, `metrics --csv` over core | `observatory-cli <cmd>` | Rule 2: the first thing that works; rule 5: what CI runs; the validators' oracle for every milestone. |
397→| `apps/observatory-app` | Tauri 2 shell (`src-tauri`) + Leptos CSR UI (`src`) | Tauri commands and events, serde types imported from core | One language, no bindings drift (PRD §12). Commands are the only boundary the UI crosses, so a TypeScript UI could replace it without touching core. |
398→
399→Tauri commands (M1 onward): `open_replay(path)`, `list_sessions()`, `attach(session_id)`,
400→`event_raw(ptr)`, `host_launch(cfg)`, `host_control(cmd)`, `metrics(scope)`, `gate(mission)`,
401→`merge(pr, target)`, `telemetry_status()`. Events from shell to UI: `events_appended(batch)`,
402→`session_discovered`, `stall_flag`, `gate_changed`. Batches flush every 100 ms (reason: well under
403→the 1 s requirement, avoids one render per line).
404→
405→### 5.2 Canonical event and lane mapping
406→
407→`Event`, `ReworkWindow`, `Lane`, `Role`, `EventKind` as in PRD appendix A; `EventKind` has one
408→variant per PRD §7 kind in `CamelCase` plus `Unknown { raw_type }`. `source: SourcePtr::Jsonl {
409→path, byte_offset, byte_len }` (appendix A has `path, byte_offset`; `byte_len` is added so a line
410→can be read without scanning for the newline) is the only thing the store keeps of a raw line
411→(PRD §11.2: the lane is a view). `mapping_version: MappingVersion` is a second addition to
412→appendix A: every `Event` names the mapper that produced it, so the first Droid upgrade shows as a
413→rising unknown-event count against a known version, never as a silently broken board (owner,
414→entry 23). Mapping is a module `mapping::v1` with a `MappingVersion`
415→selected from the Droid version in the session `.settings.json`; unknown Droid versions use the
416→latest mapping and raise a one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18
417→covers the rest). A mapping version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets
418→`mapping::v2` and its own fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the
419→contract of a version.
420→
421→### 5.3 Store schema
422→
423→SQLite via `rusqlite` with the `bundled` feature (reason: core is sync, a desktop index needs no
424→async driver, and bundling removes the system-library dependency from the clean-clone rule).
425→File: `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` (schema version table, migrations forward-only).
426→
427→| Table | Columns (keys) | Note |
428→|---|---|---|
429→| `sessions` | `id`, `path`, `droid_version`, `tag`, `role`, `parent_id`, `mission_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at` | One row per JSONL file; `tag` confirmed in M0 |
430→| `events` | `id`, `session_id`, `mission_id`, `milestone_id`, `feature_id`, `lane`, `kind`, `raw_type`, `mapping_version`, `role`, `model`, `at`, `duration_ms`, `path`, `byte_offset`, `byte_len` | Pointer, never payload |
431→| `usage` | `event_id`, `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `credits` | From `usage.reported` |
432→| `missions`, `milestones`, `features` | ids, names, `defined_at`, `completed_at`, `state` | Board model |
433→| `rework_windows` | `feature_id`, `opened_by`, `closed_by`, `cause` | PRD §10.2 |
434→| `prs`, `checks`, `attestations`, `reviews` | GitHub ids, state, `observed_at`, `url` | Lane 8 |
435→| `human_actions` | `id`, `kind`, `target`, `at`, `payload_ptr` | Lane 7 |
436→| `prices` | `effective`, `model`, `class`, `per_m`, `source` | Loaded from the dated TOML |
437→| `mapping_versions` | `version`, `droid_version_range`, `frozen_at` | §5.2 |
438→
439→Raw lines are read on demand from `path`+`byte_offset`; if the file moved, the UI says so and
440→shows the pointer (reason: never copy raw lines, PRD §11.2).

442→### 5.4 Ingest adapters behind traits
443→
444→```rust
445→pub trait Source { fn poll(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>>; fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind; }
446→pub trait Forge  { fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>>;
447→                   fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>>; fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy>;
448→                   fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged>; /* attestations, reviews */ }
449→```
450→
451→`JsonlSource` (attach; replay = the same source at end of file with a clock the scrubber drives),
452→`RpcSource` (host, M2), `GitSource` (M4), `GitHubSource: Forge` (M4). Reason: one adapter for
453→attach and replay removes a whole class of "works in replay, not live" bugs (D-008); the `Forge`
454→trait is the seam for other forges later (PRD §5 non-goal, §11.2).

475→### 5.6 Metric definitions
476→
477→By reference, not restated: time states PRD §10.1, rework windows §10.2, mission overhead §10.3,
478→cycle/waste/bottleneck/fix loops §10.4, cost §10.5. Closed cause lists used by the engine and the
479→exporter: **waste causes** `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`,
480→`waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled` (8);
481→**rework causes** `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate` (4). Mission overhead is a
482→separate line in the app and is not exported (reason: it belongs to no card and D-010 has no label
483→for it). The CSV export has one row per feature with every §10.4 measure and the price-table date.
484→
485→### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)
486→
487→Contract: OTLP `http/protobuf` to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp`; header
488→value only from the keychain item `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`; resource attributes
489→`service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`; labels only from `mission`, `milestone`,
490→`role`, `model`, `cause`; counters and histograms only; one mission exported at a time.
491→
492→| Metric | Instrument | Labels | Cardinality (worst case) | Series |
493→|---|---|---|---|---|
494→| `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 6 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (6 + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) | 9 |
495→| `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 5 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (5 + 3) | 8 |
496→| `observatory.waste_seconds` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 milestones × 8 causes | 64 |
497→| `observatory.rework_windows` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 × 4 | 32 |
498→| `observatory.fix_loops` | counter | `mission`, `milestone` | 8 | 8 |
499→| `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}` | 4 counters | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 3 roles × 4 models = 12 pairs × 4 | 48 |
500→| `observatory.cost_usd` | counter | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 12 | 12 |
501→| `observatory.unknown_events` | counter | `mission` | 1 | 1 |
502→| **Total worst case** | | | | **182** |
503→
504→Expected for this mission (7 milestones, 3 role×model pairs): 9 + 8 + 56 + 28 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 1 =
505→**124**. Both are strictly under 200. Why these shapes: the feature-cycle histogram carries no
506→`milestone` label because a histogram per milestone (7 series each) would cost 56 series for a
507→distribution the app already shows per card; waste and rework keep `milestone` because the budget
508→meter and the waste chart are read per card. Guards: the `milestone` label is bounded by
509→`max_milestone_labels` (the ninth and later milestones of any observed mission export as
510→`milestone="overflow"`); `role` is the closed `Role` enum; `model` beyond four distinct values per
511→mission exports as `model="other"`; the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case for the
512→configured buckets and limits is not under `[telemetry].max_series`, and the test
513→`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins the 182. Series of a previous
514→mission stop being written when the export target changes; `mission_switch_min_interval_min` keeps
515→the two sets from overlapping inside Grafana's active-series window. A `service.version` change
516→(release) re-keys the resource once; it is not a steady-state cost. CI telemetry stays deferred
517→(B-002). D-010 sized the shape at up to 6 milestones; this spec uses 8 label values because the
518→skeleton makes seven milestones and one `overflow` value bounds other missions. Still under 200.
519→
520→### 5.8 Runtime limits
521→
522→From §5.5: 64 watched sessions, 512 MB per session file before warnings, 1 MiB tail chunk,
523→100 ms UI batch, 500 ms JSONL poll, 30 s GitHub poll, 15 s metric export, 20 min stall threshold.
524→The UI holds at most the visible window of events; everything else is a store query (reason: a
525→mission can emit tens of thousands of lines; the board must stay at 60 fps on a laptop). The host
526→child process is reaped on window close (M2 test). No network access except GitHub (when a token
527→is present) and the OTLP gateway (when enabled); both are shown in a status bar.
528→
529→Validation and build concurrency (measured 2026-10-22; source:
530→`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`):
531→
532→- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
533→  CPU negligible idle).
534→- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
535→- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
536→  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`).
537→- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141.
538→- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.

540→### 5.9 Security
541→
542→- Secrets only from the macOS keychain or the environment (rule 4): `droid-observatory/github-token`
543→  or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for lane 8; `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` for telemetry (no environment
544→  fallback in the app, D-010). Never in config, store, logs or the exported telemetry.
545→- Raw JSONL is rendered read-only after the B-006 scrub pass, never uploaded, never copied into the
546→  store (PRD §11.2); rendering read-only and the merge as the one outward write are PRD §11.3.
547→  Fixtures are committed only after gitleaks and a human read (§3).
548→- The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5): confirmation names PR number and target branch;
549→  the app uses the repository's allowed merge method; the action is a lane-7 event.
550→- Telemetry carries no session id, event id, feature id or free text (D-010); the label allow-list
551→  is enforced in code and by test.

553→## 6. Tests
554→
555→Fixtures are captured streams, named and dated (§3). Local = `make check` in a worktree; MB = the
556→`mission-checks` aggregate on `mission/**`; PR = the `gate` aggregate on the final pull request.
557→
558→| Suite | Covers | Where | Command |
559→|---|---|---|---|
560→| Unit (`#[cfg(test)]` next to code) | model, mapping helpers, time-state engine, windows, cost, label allow-list | local, MB, PR | `cargo test --workspace --all-features` |
561→| Fixture replay (`crates/observatory-core/tests/replay_*.rs`, `mapping.rs`) | each fixture → golden lane events, `unknown events: 0` on frozen captures | local, MB, PR | `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` |
562→| Attach latency (`tests/attach_latency.rs`) | harness appends a fixture line by line; event visible to the store within 1 s | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test attach_latency` |
563→| CLI (`crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`) | exit codes, `unknown events: N` line, `inspect` prints the exact raw line | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-cli` |
564→| Metrics oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, M5) | engine output vs `reports/reference/*.csv` within tolerance | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` |
565→| Telemetry budget (M5) | worst-case series count = 182 < 200; labels outside the set rejected | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
566→| UI logic | view-model functions (card position, filters, scrubber) live in core and are unit-tested there; the Leptos layer holds no logic worth a wasm test runner (reason: `wasm-bindgen-test` adds a toolchain step for little coverage) | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
567→| Interactive QA (validators) | board, Details, tray, filters, scrubber in the **browser host** `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker; attach, host, controls and gate in the **Tauri window** (`make app-dev`) with screenshots and the CLI as oracle | per milestone, by the user-testing validator | `make app-dev`; `trunk serve --port 3141` |
568→| Coverage (B-005) | `observatory-core` lines | S: reported; **M0 onward: fail under 80 %**; MB and PR | `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` |
569→
570→**B-005 settled: 80 % lines on `observatory-core`.** Reason: core holds every piece of logic that
571→can be wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost), so it is where coverage buys correctness;
572→IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub are in core too and cannot all be exercised in CI,
573→which is the 20 % of room. The CLI is thin and covered by its own tests without a threshold; the
574→UI crate is excluded (wasm target, no logic). Enforced from M0 integration because S has too little
575→code for a percentage to mean anything. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason, lowering it is
576→a decision file.

578→## 7. CI
579→
580→Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
581→pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).
582→
583→**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
584→`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
585→decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
586→`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
587→**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
588→rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
589→warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
590→decision file.
591→
592→**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
593→in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
594→finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.
595→
596→**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
597→label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
598→`main`.
599→
600→**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
601→ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan of
602→the repository (vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH and CRITICAL; `Cargo.lock` is what makes the vuln
603→scan meaningful), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`)
604→with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy results and SBOM
605→attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the human to a
606→commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and, from S onward, checks the workspace version against the
607→tag (B-016, wired in S; D-009).

1→# PRD: droid-observatory
2→
3→| Field | Value |
4→|---|---|
5→| Status | Draft v0.6 for review |
6→| Date | 2026-10-22 |
7→| Owner | dct |
8→| Author | Droid (ideation session, see `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md`) |
9→| Changes from v0.1 to v0.6 | See Appendix C |
10→
11→---
12→
13→## 1. Summary
14→
15→droid-observatory is a Rust desktop application that shows how a Factory Mission moves through the engineering build cycle. It renders the mission as a board whose lanes are the orchestrated states of a mission, from the human's intent through orchestration, building, validation, integration, the human gate, and the outside ecosystem (PR, CI, deploy). Alongside the flow it measures what the flow costs: cycle time, waste by cause, tokens and money per sub-droid and per model.
16→
17→The observatory attaches to missions started from any terminal on this machine (it watches `~/.factory/sessions/` and tails each new session file as it grows), replays finished ones from the same files, and can also host a mission itself (it spawns `droid exec --mission` and consumes the JSON-RPC event stream, which adds the control channel). Attach is the primary live mode; hosting is the secondary path. It never copies the event data into a second source of truth: every lane entry is a view over the raw JSONL line it came from.
18→
19→A mission is not complete when the workers stop. It is complete when the gate is green and the merge has happened.
20→
21→## 2. Delivery model
22→
23→This section defines the units the board shows. Everything else follows from it.
24→
25→- **A mission is a business feature: the unit that ships.** For this project, v1 of the observatory. A mission ends in **one PR into `main`**, outcome-sized, with the evidence attached. The full attested CI runs on that PR; CD runs from `main`.
26→- **Milestones are internal iterations**, not shippable. Each milestone runs in its own worktree and is integrated into a **`mission/<name>` branch**, the mission's interface to `main`. Fast checks (tests, lint, the gate command) run on that branch to keep it healthy. Nothing on it is shippable or pretends to be.
27→- **The mission branch is short-lived by construction.** It dies at the merge. That is what keeps it from becoming a long-lived `dev` branch.
28→- **Features** are the orchestrator's work items inside a milestone. Workers build them, validators judge them, and metrics are computed at feature granularity, then rolled up to the milestone and the mission.
29→- **The fix loop after CI red reopens the mission on its branch.** It does not open a new PR. The same PR goes green or stays red.
30→
31→On the board: **cards are milestones**; the gate group in lane 8 is the mission's one PR; lane 6 is integration into `mission/<name>`; lane 8 is the PR.
32→
33→**Models per role** (decision D-006; `ai/RULES.md` rule 19): orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`. Reasoning effort per role is declared in the spec. A change of model is a decision file.
34→
35→The orchestrator catalog ID spelling was corrected on 2026-10-22 (D-006); Appendix C retains the historical spelling.
36→
37→## 3. Problem
38→
39→Mission Control (CLI and Factory App) shows progress, workers, and a log. It does not show:
40→
41→- the mission's full life, including what happens after the workers stop (PR, CI, attestations, deploy, red builds that need a fix);
42→- where time goes: active work versus waiting on a human, waiting on validation, waiting on merge, rework after a blocking finding, retries and conflicts;
43→- what each role and model consumed, so that model and reasoning-effort choices can be compared with real numbers;
44→- a single place to act when the mission needs a human: approve, answer, redirect, merge.
45→
46→Running missions without that view means managing agents blind on the two dimensions that matter most for an engineering organization: flow and cost.
47→
48→## 4. Goals
49→
50→1. Show every milestone of a mission across the nine lanes defined in section 7, live and in replay, with features visible inside each card.
51→2. Show per card: validation state (red/green), current agent, gate state, and a Details view with review notes, validation criteria, commits, and raw event links.
52→3. Let the human act from the board: pause/resume the orchestrator, send instructions, answer escalations, approve, mark a feature complete or skipped, and merge the PR when policy says a human merges.
53→4. Measure cycle time, waste by cause, mission overhead, and bottlenecks per feature, per milestone, per role, and per mission.
54→5. Measure cost: tokens per sub-droid, converted to Factory Standard Credits when the stream exposes them, otherwise money via a dated price table that every displayed cost references.
55→6. Treat CI red on the mission PR as a counted rework loop: reopen the mission on its branch, loop the affected card back into the Workers lane, keep the same PR.
56→
57→## 5. Non-goals (v1)
58→
59→- Replacing Mission Control for planning. The observatory starts after a plan exists (it may launch the mission, but the plan conversation stays in Droid).
60→- Multi-user or server deployment. v1 is a single-user desktop app reading local data and the user's own GitHub access.
61→- Writing to Factory's hosted API beyond what the local `droid` process already does.
62→- Editing code or reviewing diffs inside the app. It links out to the worktree, commit, or PR.
63→- Supporting CI systems other than GitHub Actions in v1 (adapter boundary is defined so others can follow).
64→
65→## 6. Users
66→
67→**Mission owner (primary).** The engineer acting as project manager of agents. Wants to see progress, act when needed, and know what the mission cost in time and money.
68→
69→**Reviewer / gatekeeper.** Opens the Details view, reads scrutiny findings and QA results, watches the outcome video, and merges or sends back.
70→
71→**Engineering lead (reader).** Compares missions and models over time: cycle time, waste, cost per feature. Does not intervene.
72→
73→## 7. Lanes
74→
75→The board has nine lanes. Lanes 1–6 are fed by the mission stream, 7–8 by GitHub and human actions, 9 by session metadata. Each event carries `session_id`, `role`, `model`, `timestamp`, `duration`, and a pointer to its raw JSONL line.
76→
77→| # | Lane | What it holds | Source | Event kinds |
78→|---|---|---|---|---|
79→| 1 | **Intent** | Mission prompt, spec, acceptance criteria; later human re-prompts | stream (user ↔ orchestrator), mission file | `intent.created`, `intent.amended`, `question.asked` (orchestrator → human), `intent.answered`, `spec.versioned` |
80→| 2 | **Orchestrator** | Plan, feature breakdown, milestones, task assignment, replans | stream (orchestrator session) | `plan.created`, `feature.defined`, `milestone.defined`, `task.assigned`, `task.skipped`, `plan.revised`, `escalation.raised`, `milestone.completed`, `mission.paused`, `mission.resumed`, `mission.completed`, `context.compacted` |
81→| 3 | **Workers** | One sub-lane per worker (or per feature when the mission names them) | stream (worker child sessions) | `subagent.spawned`, `task.started`, `file.touched`, `tests.run`, `commit.created`, `task.done`, `subagent.finished`, `tool.error`, `permission.requested`, `permission.granted`, `permission.denied`, `hook.blocked`, `usage.reported`, `model.changed` |
82→| 4 | **Validators, scrutiny** | Review findings, blocking vs non-blocking, re-work requested and resolved | stream (scrutiny validator sessions) | `finding.blocking`, `finding.non_blocking`, `rework.requested`, `rework.resolved`, `scrutiny.passed` |
83→| 5 | **Validators, user testing** | QA runs against the built thing, scenario results | stream (user-testing validator sessions) | `qa.scenario.passed`, `qa.scenario.failed`, `qa.evidence` (screenshot, video) |
84→| 6 | **Integration** | Worktree merges into `mission/<name>`, conflicts, fast checks. Wording is "integrated in mission", never "merged" | stream (orchestrator/worker git activity) | `integration.merged`, `integration.conflict`, `integration.conflict_resolved`, `gate_command.run`, `gate_command.passed`, `gate_command.failed` |
85→| 7 | **Human** | Approvals, answers to escalations, review of the outcome (the video), the merge of the PR | app actions, stream attention events | `approval.requested`, `approval.given`, `question.answered`, `review.outcome`, `pr.merged_by_human` |
86→| 8 | **Outside** | The mission PR into `main`: opened, reviews, checks, attestations, merge, deploys. Empty for the observatory itself until its final PR | GitHub adapter | `pr.opened`, `pr.review_requested`, `check.started`, `check.passed`, `check.failed`, `check.required_missing`, `ruleset.blocked`, `attestation.recorded`, `attestation.verified`, `pr.merged_by_policy`, `deploy.completed` |
87→| 9 | **Time, Waste, Cost and models** | Tokens and usage per role, which model did what; budget meter; elapsed, stuck, and wasted time; mission overhead | derived from all lanes + session metadata | computed, not evented |
88→
89→**`unknown.event`** is a first-class kind in every lane. It is counted, surfaced in an "unmapped" tray, and never dropped. M0's exit criterion is driving its count to zero on the capture.
90→
91→Lane 9 is rendered as a panel that doubles as the mission's budget meter. It is the lane the other eight are measured against.
92→
93→`context.compacted` is kept in lane 2 because it explains sudden quality drops in the sessions that follow it. `hook.blocked` is the write guard firing; it is counted under retry and failure.
94→
95→## 8. Board model
96→
97→**Card = one milestone.** The milestone is the spec phase: the orchestrator plans it, workers build its features in a worktree, validators judge it, and it integrates into `mission/<name>`. Each card lists its features with their individual state, and metrics roll up feature → milestone → mission.
98→
99→A card moves left to right. Its position is the lane where its most recent open activity is. The Details view shows the full history across lanes.
100→
101→**Gate group.** Lane 8 holds one group per mission: the mission PR. All cards of the mission share that gate state; the badge sits on the group. Until the PR exists, lane 8 shows the mission branch with its fast-check status as a pre-gate placeholder.
102→
103→**Fix loop.** When CI goes red on the mission PR, the observatory reopens the mission on `mission/<name>` with a cycle tagged `fix` on the milestone(s) whose features the fix touches. Those cards are drawn with a loop arrow back into lane 3. The PR stays the same. The loop is counted as rework in lane 9.
104→
105→**Mission completion.** Mission state is `complete` only when the PR is merged with CI green. Until then it is `planning`, `building`, `validating`, `at gate`, or `fixing`.
106→
107→### 8.1 Card anatomy
108→
109→```text
110→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
111→│ M2  Host                                    [Details]│
112→│ features 4/6 done · worktree wt/m2 · mission/obs-v1  │
113→│ ● validation: RED (1 blocking)  ◆ branch: fast checks ✓│
114→│ now: worker-3 (claude-sonnet-5-5) on F-014 · 00:14:22 │
115→│ cycle 2h 10m · waste 38m (rework 22m, human 16m)      │
116→│ 412k tok · $1.84 (prices 2026-10-22)                  │
117→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
118→
119→Gate group (lane 8):
120→┌── PR #41  mission/observatory-v1 → main ─────────────┐
121→│ ◆ gate: HUMAN REQUIRED · checks 7/7 ✓ · attested ✓     │
122→│ cards: M0 M1 M2 M3 M4 M5                      [Merge]  │
123→└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
124→```
125→
126→- **Validation badge** (card): GREEN when scrutiny passed and user-testing scenarios passed for all features on the latest build; RED when any blocking finding or failed scenario is open; GREY when not yet validated.
127→- **Branch badge** (card): fast checks on `mission/<name>` passed / failed / running for this milestone's integration.
128→- **Gate badge** (group): `pending` (no PR), `checks running`, `review requested`, `human required`, `ruleset blocked`, `policy-merged`, `CI green`, `CI red`.
129→- **Now**: the agent currently holding a feature of this card (role, model, session id, feature, time on task). Empty when idle, with the idle reason (waiting on human, waiting on validation, queued).
130→- **Merge** button (group): only visible when the gate policy requires a human merge and checks are green.
131→
132→## 9. Functional requirements
133→
134→### 9.1 Board (FR-B)
135→
136→- FR-B1: Render the nine lanes with milestone cards positioned by current lane.
137→- FR-B2: Lane 3 shows sub-lanes per worker, or per feature when the mission names them. Toggle between the two groupings.
138→- FR-B3: Lane 8 shows the mission PR as one gate group containing all cards; before the PR exists, it shows the mission branch with fast-check status.
139→- FR-B4: Fix loops are drawn as a visible return arc from lane 8 to lane 3 on the affected card(s), with the cycle count on the card.
140→- FR-B5: Filter by milestone, feature, role, model, validation state, gate state.
141→- FR-B6: Live mode updates within 1 s of the event arriving; replay mode has a time scrubber.
142→- FR-B7: An "unmapped" tray shows the count of `unknown.event` and opens their raw lines.
143→
144→### 9.2 Details (FR-D)
145→
146→Opened via the Details button on a card. Tabs:
147→
148→- FR-D1 **Timeline**: every event for the milestone and its features across all lanes, each with role, model, duration, and a link that opens the raw JSONL line.
149→- FR-D2 **Review notes**: scrutiny findings (blocking / non-blocking, status: open / resolved), user-testing scenario results with evidence (screenshots, video).
150→- FR-D3 **Validation criteria**: the acceptance criteria from the plan, per feature, and which events satisfied each.
151→- FR-D4 **Commits and integration**: commits, worktree, integration into `mission/<name>`, conflicts, fast-check results.
152→- FR-D5 **Gate**: mission PR link, reviews, checks, attestations, merge policy and which rule decided, merge history.
153→- FR-D6 **Cost and waste**: per-feature and per-role token and cost breakdown for this milestone, waste split by cause, rework windows listed.
154→
155→### 9.3 Agent attribution (FR-A)
156→
157→- FR-A1: Show which agent (role, session id, model) is working on each feature now, surfaced on the card.
158→- FR-A2: Agent panel lists all orchestrator, worker, and validator sessions with status (active, idle, waiting, finished), current feature, model, and tokens so far.
159→- FR-A3: Selecting an agent shows its live output stream.
160→- FR-A4: `model.changed` and `context.compacted` are marked on the agent's timeline.
161→
162→### 9.4 Human intervention (FR-H)
163→
164→All actions are logged as lane 7 events with the human as actor.
165→
166→- FR-H1: Pause / resume the orchestrator.
167→- FR-H2: Send a message to the orchestrator (redirect, re-plan request, scope change).
168→- FR-H3: Answer an open question or approve/deny a permission request raised by any sub-droid.
169→- FR-H4: Mark a feature complete or skipped (relayed to the orchestrator as an instruction).
170→- FR-H5: Stall detection: a feature with no active time for a configurable threshold is flagged; the flag suggests the matching troubleshooting prompt (frozen mission, stuck worker, repeated failure).
171→- FR-H6: Interventions are expected to be rare. The UI must not nudge the user to intervene when the mission is progressing (no alerts on normal waits under threshold).
172→
173→### 9.5 Mission branch and gate (FR-G)
174→
175→- FR-G1: Identify the mission branch `mission/<name>` and the worktree of each milestone.
176→- FR-G2: Record fast-check runs on the mission branch as lane 6 `gate_command.*` events, attributed to the milestone being integrated.
177→- FR-G3: Detect the mission PR (`mission/<name>` → `main`) when it opens; poll check runs, required checks, reviews, rulesets, and attestations.
178→- FR-G4: Read the merge policy for `main` (GitHub branch protection / rulesets plus an app-level override) and decide whether a human merge is required. Show which rule decided.
179→- FR-G5: When a human merge is required and checks are green, show the Merge button on the gate group. Merge via GitHub API with the repository's allowed merge method. Confirm before merging, naming PR and target branch.
180→- FR-G6: When policy merges automatically, flip the badge to `policy-merged` on detection.
181→- FR-G7: On CI red, reopen the mission on `mission/<name>` with a `fix` cycle on the affected milestone(s); no new PR. If the orchestrator is still running, instruct it; if it has ended, launch a follow-up mission on the same branch pre-filled with the feature spec, failing check output, and original session ids.
182→- FR-G8: On merge, mark the mission `complete` and record that the mission branch is to be deleted (or detect its deletion).
183→
184→### 9.6 Metrics (FR-M)
185→
186→Definitions in section 10. All metrics are available per feature, per milestone, per role, per model, and per mission, and exportable as CSV/JSON.
187→
188→- FR-M1: Cycle time per feature, per milestone, per mission, and per lane.
189→- FR-M2: Waste by cause, including waiting on merge and mission overhead reported separately.
190→- FR-M3: Bottlenecks: lanes and roles with the longest queue time and highest WIP; queued-behind-WIP idle is a bottleneck signal, unscheduled idle is not.
191→- FR-M4: Tokens per sub-droid, per model, per feature.
192→- FR-M5: Cost in Factory Standard Credits when exposed by the stream; otherwise in money from the dated price table. Every cost display shows the price-table date it used.
193→- FR-M6: Budget meter: mission cost so far against an optional budget set at launch.
194→- FR-M7: Model comparison: for the same role, cost and first-pass active time per completed feature by model.
195→
196→### 9.7 Mission lifecycle (FR-L)
197→
198→- FR-L1: Attach (primary live mode): watch `~/.factory/sessions/` with a filesystem notifier, detect any new session JSONL (a mission started from any terminal on this machine), tail it as it grows and render it within 1 s, named by its `--tag` or session id. No control channel.
199→- FR-L2: Replay a finished mission from JSONL files. Same adapter as attach: replay is attach at end-of-file, with the scrubber.
200→- FR-L3: Host (secondary path): launch a mission from the app: choose repo, mission file, mission branch name, models and reasoning effort for orchestrator / worker / validator, autonomy flags, optional budget. The app spawns `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc`; this is the only mode with a control channel (pause, message, answer).
201→- FR-L4: Mission library: list past missions with headline metrics.

203→## 10. Metric definitions
204→
205→### 10.1 Time states
206→
207→Each feature, at every instant, is in exactly one time state:
208→
209→| State | Definition |
210→|---|---|
211→| **Active** | A worker, validator, or orchestrator is doing something for the feature: tool call in flight or model generating. |
212→| **Waiting on human** | A question or approval is open and nobody is acting (lane 7 open, lanes 2–6 idle for this feature). Sub-causes: *question*, *permission*, *waiting on merge* (checks green, policy requires a human, nobody has merged). |
213→| **Waiting on validation** | Work is done, validator not started. |
214→| **Retry and failure** | Time in tool errors, `hook.blocked`, re-runs of the same command, and conflict resolution. |
215→| **Idle, queued** | Feature is planned and ready but blocked behind another feature (WIP limit, dependency, no free worker). A bottleneck signal. |
216→| **Idle, unscheduled** | Feature exists but nothing is scheduled and nothing is blocking it. Not a bottleneck signal. |
217→
218→Rework is not a separate time state. It is a window (10.2) that overlays active, retry, and waiting time.
219→
220→### 10.2 Rework windows
221→
222→A **rework window** opens at a blocking signal and closes at its resolution event, per signal:
223→
224→| Opens | Closes |
225→|---|---|
226→| `finding.blocking` | `rework.resolved` |
227→| `qa.scenario.failed` | `qa.scenario.passed` for the same scenario |
228→| `integration.conflict` | `integration.conflict_resolved` |
229→| `check.failed` (mission PR) | `check.passed` for the same check |
230→
231→Overlapping windows on the same feature merge into one. A window with no closing event stays open until mission end and is reported as unresolved.
232→
233→- **Rework time** = active time inside rework windows.
234→- **First-pass active time** = active time outside any rework window.
235→
236→This bounds rework so that legitimate new work after a fix is not counted as waste.
237→
238→### 10.3 Mission overhead
239→
240→Orchestrator time before the first `feature.defined`, replanning time not attributable to one feature, and `context.compacted` recovery belong to no card. They are reported as **mission overhead**, a separate line in lane 9, never apportioned silently. An optional explicit apportionment (equal split across features) can be switched on for comparisons and is labeled as such.
241→
242→### 10.4 Derived measures
243→
244→- **Cycle time** (feature) = `feature.defined` → feature's last `task.done` with validation green and integrated. **Cycle time** (milestone) = `milestone.defined` → `milestone.completed`. **Cycle time** (mission) = `intent.created` → `pr.merged` (human or policy) with CI green. Stage cycle times are computed per lane.
245→- **Waste** = total elapsed − first-pass active time, split by cause: waiting on human (question, permission, merge), waiting on validation, rework, retry and failure, idle queued, idle unscheduled. Mission overhead is reported next to waste, not inside it. Reported per feature, per milestone, and per role.
246→- **Bottleneck** = lane or role with the highest sum of waiting plus queued time across features in the window, and the lane with the highest WIP relative to its throughput.
247→- **Fix loops** = count of `fix` cycles per milestone and per mission.
248→
249→### 10.5 Cost
250→
251→- Token counts are taken from `usage.reported` events per session (input, output, cache read, cache write when available).
252→- If the stream reports Factory Standard Credits, credits are the primary unit.
253→- Otherwise cost = Σ tokens × price per model and token class, from the **price table**: a dated config file (`~/.droid-observatory/prices/<YYYY-MM-DD>.toml`). The board always shows the date of the table it used, and a mission keeps the table it started with unless the user re-prices it explicitly.
254→- Cost is shown next to waste so that a slow, cheap model and a fast, expensive one can be compared on the same panel.
255→
256→Price table example (values illustrative, table dated):
257→
258→```toml
259→# ~/.droid-observatory/prices/2026-10-22.toml
260→effective = "2026-10-22"
261→currency = "USD"
262→
263→[models."claude-fable-5.1"]
264→input_per_m = 0.0
265→output_per_m = 0.0
266→cache_read_per_m = 0.0
267→cache_write_per_m = 0.0
268→
269→[models."claude-opus-5-5"]
270→input_per_m = 0.0
271→output_per_m = 0.0
272→
273→[models."claude-sonnet-5-5"]

276→

281→
282→The shipped default table carries the vendor prices on its date; the user edits and re-dates it.

284→## 11. Data sources and architecture
285→
286→### 11.1 Sources
287→
288→| Source | Mode | Provides |
289→|---|---|---|
290→| `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl` (+ `.settings.json`), watched | **Attach (primary live mode)** | The observatory watches `~/.factory/sessions/` with a filesystem notifier, detects any new session JSONL (a mission started from any terminal on this machine), tails it as it grows and renders it in real time, named by its `--tag` or session id. Worker and validator events via the child session files. These are the canonical raw lines that lane entries link to. Read-only: no control channel. |
291→| Same files, finished | Replay | Same adapter: replay is attach at end-of-file, plus the time scrubber. |
292→| `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc` | Host (secondary live mode) | Every orchestrator event; token usage; permission and question requests; the control channel (pause, message, answer). Started from the app's launch screen. |
293→| Git (local) | Live, polled | Mission branch, milestone worktrees, integration commits, fast-check results. |
294→| GitHub REST/GraphQL (user token) | Live, polled | The mission PR, reviews, check runs, required checks, rulesets, attestations, merges, deploy statuses. |
295→| App actions | Live | Lane 7 human events. |
296→
297→Attach is primary because missions are started from the terminal in practice; the launch screen is the secondary path. Hosting is the only mode with a control channel; attach and replay are read-only views over the same files.
298→
299→Open items: the exact JSON-RPC event schema for missions (how worker child sessions, feature ids, milestone ids, and validator roles are identified) is not fully documented, and where `--tag` is recorded (session settings file or first stream line) is unconfirmed. M0 captures a real mission stream, confirms both, and freezes the mapping from raw events to lane events as a versioned module with fixtures.
300→
301→### 11.2 Components
302→
303→```text
304→┌─────────────────────────── Tauri 2 shell ───────────────────────────┐
305→│  UI (webview)                                                        │
306→│   board · details · agents · metrics · launch · settings            │
307→└──────────────▲───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
308→               │ Tauri commands + events (serde types shared with core)
309→┌──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
310→│ observatory-core (Rust lib)                                          │
311→│  ingest/   jsonl_watch · jsonl_tail (attach; replay = attach at EOF) │
312→│            droid_rpc (host) · git · github                           │
313→│  model/    Event · Feature · Milestone · Agent · Lane mapping        │
314→│            (versioned by Droid version)                              │
315→│  metrics/  time states · rework windows · overhead · cycle · waste · │
316→│            bottleneck · cost                                         │
317→│  store/    SQLite index: events(ptr→jsonl file,offset), features,    │
318→│            milestones, agents, pr, checks, prices                    │
319→│  control/  pause · message · answer · mark · merge                   │
320→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
321→```
322→
323→- **The lane is a view, not a copy.** The store indexes events with a pointer to the raw JSONL line (file, byte offset). Opening an event in the UI reads the raw line on demand.
324→- `observatory-core` has no UI dependency and is testable from fixtures (recorded mission streams). A thin CLI (`observatory replay <session>`) exercises it headlessly and is the first thing that works.
325→- The GitHub adapter is behind a trait so other forges and CI systems can follow.
326→
327→### 11.3 Security
328→
329→- GitHub token and Factory credentials stay in the OS keychain (Tauri keyring plugin). Never written to the store or logs.
330→- Raw JSONL may contain secrets from tool output; the app renders it read-only and never uploads it.
331→- Merge is the only outward-facing write. It requires an explicit confirmation naming the PR and target branch.
332→
333→### 11.4 Telemetry export (Grafana Cloud)
334→
335→Two kinds of telemetry leave the app, both over OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to a Grafana Cloud stack, both off by default so the app works fully offline (decision D-004):
336→
337→- **App telemetry**: `tracing` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics, and control; errors as span events.
338→- **Mission metrics**: the lane-9 series, so the budget meter and waste can be charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. Metric names are a contract: `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds`, `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds`, `observatory.waste_seconds`, `observatory.rework_windows`, `observatory.fix_loops`, `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}`, `observatory.cost_usd`, `observatory.unknown_events`.
339→
340→Contract (owner, D-010): OTLP over HTTP to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp` (`/v1/metrics`, `/v1/traces`, `/v1/logs`). The `Authorization=Basic …` header value is read at runtime from the macOS keychain item with service `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` and account = current user; never written to config, the store or logs; if the item is missing, telemetry stays off and the UI says so. Resource attributes: `service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`. Metric labels only from `mission`, `milestone`, `role`, `model`, `cause`; never session id, event id or free text. Counters and histograms only, no per-event gauges. The spec states the number of active series the app adds and keeps it under 200 (B-017). Config keys and defaults: `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`. CI telemetry is deferred (B-002).

342→## 12. Technology options and recommendation
343→
344→Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. Needs: data-dense board, live updates, charts, markdown and video rendering in Details, long-lived subprocess management, SQLite.
345→
346→| Option | Pros | Cons |
347→|---|---|---|
348→| **A. Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust, CSR via Trunk)** | Single language; shared serde types between core and UI with no bindings; fine-grained reactivity suits a live board; webview gives markdown, video, CSS layout for free. | Charting ecosystem thinner than JS; WASM/Trunk toolchain adds build steps; smaller community. **Droids have far less Leptos in their training than React or Svelte**, so worker rework on UI tasks is likely higher. **The WASM/Trunk toolchain inside a Mission is a new failure mode** (toolchain install, target, dev server) that validators may struggle to diagnose. |
349→| B. Tauri 2 + Dioxus | Same single-language benefit; React-like ergonomics; growing fast. | Dioxus also ships its own desktop renderer, which blurs the "why Tauri" story; same training-data and toolchain concerns as A. |
350→| C. Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte or React) | Richest charting and UI libraries; fastest to a polished UI; best-known stack for Droids. | Two languages; types must be generated (ts-rs/specta) and kept in sync; the user's stated preference is Rust. |
351→| D. iced (native) | Pure Rust, no webview, small binary, Elm architecture fits an event-driven board. | Markdown, video, and rich text are weak; complex layouts cost more effort; no Tauri plugin ecosystem (keyring, updater, tray). |
352→| E. egui (native, immediate mode) | Trivial live updates and plots (egui_plot); excellent for dashboards. | Looks like a tool, not an app; text-heavy Details view (review notes, markdown) is awkward; accessibility and theming limited. |
353→
354→**Recommendation: Option A, Tauri 2 + Leptos, with M1 as an explicit go/no-go.**
355→
356→Reasoning: the hard part of this product is `observatory-core` (ingest, mapping, metrics), not the UI. Keeping the UI in Rust means the metric types, lane mapping, and event model are used directly in the view with no translation layer, which is where drift and bugs would otherwise appear. The webview covers the rich-content needs (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering) that native options handle poorly. Charting is the one real gap; lane 9 needs stacked bars and timelines, achievable as SVG from Leptos signals, with a JS chart library as a documented escape hatch.
357→
358→**Go/no-go criterion (evaluated at M1 completion):** the board renders the M0 replay (all nine lanes, cards positioned correctly, Details timeline open) with **at most 3 worker sessions of rework** after the first scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented command. If either fails, switch to Option C for M2 onward, keeping `observatory-core` unchanged; the Tauri command boundary is designed to make that swap possible. (Threshold of 3 agreed 2026-10-22; may be adjusted at planning time.)

361→
362→**One mission, six milestones, one branch `mission/observatory-v1`, one PR at the end.** Each milestone runs in its own worktree and integrates into the mission branch with fast checks. M0 must complete before the orchestrator plans M1 onward in detail, because the stream schema is unknown until the capture exists.
363→
364→| # | Name | Outcome | Validation |
365→|---|---|---|---|
366→| M0 | Stream capture and mapping | Capture one real mission run (`droid exec --mission` on a sample repo); write the raw→lane event mapper with fixtures; `observatory replay` CLI prints lane events. Freeze the mapping, versioned by Droid version. | Fixture tests pass; `unknown.event` count on the capture is zero; every event kind in section 7 that appears in the capture is mapped. **Gate for planning M1–M5 in detail.** |
367→| M1 | Board in replay and attach | Tauri 2 + Leptos app renders the nine lanes and milestone cards from a session JSONL; Details timeline tab; scrubber; unmapped tray. Attach: a filesystem watcher on `~/.factory/sessions/` detects any new session file, tails it as it grows and renders it live, named by its `--tag` or session id; replay is attach at end-of-file, same adapter. Agent panel with current agent per feature; `model.changed` and `context.compacted` markers. | Replay of the M0 capture shows all milestones and features with correct lane positions versus the capture's known outcome. A mission started in a terminal appears on the board, and each of its events shows, within 1 s. Agent attribution matches orchestrator logs. **Leptos go/no-go evaluated here (section 12).** |
368→| M2 | Host | Launch screen (secondary path); spawn `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc` from the app; pause, message and answer controls over the RPC input channel; live output per agent from the host stream. | A hosted mission shows events within 1 s; pause, message and answer reach the orchestrator and its reaction appears on the board; the same mission attached from its JSONL shows the same lane events. |
369→| M3 | Intervention | Lane 7 semantics for every control (M2 pause/resume, message, answer; plus approve/deny, mark complete/skipped); stall flag with suggested prompts. | Each action produces a lane 7 event and the orchestrator reacts. |
370→| M4 | Mission branch, gate, and fix loop | Git adapter (mission branch, worktrees, fast checks → lane 6); GitHub adapter; gate group in lane 8; gate badge; merge policy with rule attribution; Merge button; CI red → `fix` cycle on the affected card, same PR. | Tested against a **demo branch pair in this repository**: `demo/base` with its own ruleset, PRs from `demo/*`, `demo-gate.yml` controlled by the `demo:red` label; no separate repository, nothing touches `main`. A red check on the demo PR opens a fix cycle; a green check with human policy shows Merge; merging via the app updates the badge. |

377→## 14. Risks and open questions
378→
379→| Risk / question | Mitigation |
380→|---|---|
381→| Mission JSON-RPC event schema is not fully documented; mapping to features, milestones, and validator roles may be heuristic. | M0 captures and freezes a versioned mapping with fixtures; `unknown.event` is counted and shown, never dropped; M0 is the gate before detailed planning. |
382→| Leptos: less Droid training data than React/Svelte; WASM/Trunk toolchain is a new failure mode inside a mission. | Core first and headless; M1 go/no-go with a written criterion; swap to TypeScript at the Tauri command boundary. |
383→| Factory Standard Credits may not be exposed per session in the stream. | Price table fallback is first-class; the UI always names the unit and the price-table date. |
384→| Attestation formats vary (GitHub artifact attestations, SLSA provenance, custom). | v1 reads GitHub artifact attestations and check-run conclusions (`attestation.recorded`), verifies via GitHub's attestation API where possible (`attestation.verified`); others appear as opaque recorded events with a link. |
385→| Merge policy lives in several places (branch protection, rulesets, CODEOWNERS, org policy). | v1 reads branch protection and rulesets, plus an explicit app-level override per repo; the Details gate tab shows which rule decided. |
386→| A `fix` cycle after the orchestrator has ended needs a follow-up mission with the right context on the same branch. | The fix launch pre-fills the mission file with the feature spec, the failing check output, the mission branch, and the original session ids. |
387→| Local JSONL files may change format between Droid versions. | The mapper is versioned by the Droid version observed in the session settings file; replay of old captures stays in the test suite. |
388→| Filesystem notifiers coalesce or miss events (macOS FSEvents latency, a session file created before the watcher starts). | The watcher is paired with a poll at `[ingest].jsonl_poll_ms`; on start the sessions directory is scanned and files already growing are attached; attach latency is measured in M1 acceptance, not assumed. |
389→| `--tag` may not be recoverable from the session files. | M0 confirms where it is recorded; if absent, sessions are named by id and the first `mission.started` payload. |
390→| M4 cannot be tested on the observatory repo itself. | The same demo branch pair in this repository (`demo/base` with its own ruleset, PRs from `demo/*`, `demo-gate.yml` controlled by the `demo:red` label), set up by the mission before M4; nothing touches `main`. |
391→| M5 has no oracle unless a human produces one. | Reference spreadsheet from the M0 capture is a listed mission input. |
392→| Webview charting in Rust is thinner than JS. | Scoped chart set (stacked bars, timeline, sparkline) built as SVG components; JS chart lib as a documented escape hatch. |

433→## Appendix B: Glossary
434→
435→- **Mission**: a business feature, the unit that ships. One PR into `main`.
436→- **Mission branch**: `mission/<name>`, the mission's interface to `main`. Short-lived; dies at the merge.
437→- **Milestone**: an internal iteration inside a mission; runs in its own worktree; integrates into the mission branch; one card.
438→- **Feature**: the orchestrator's work item inside a milestone; the granularity at which metrics are computed.
439→- **Sub-droid**: any agent session spawned for the mission: orchestrator, worker, scrutiny validator, user-testing validator.
440→- **Integration**: landing a milestone worktree on the mission branch, with fast checks. Not a merge in the gate sense.
441→- **Gate**: the mission PR into `main`, merged by a human or by policy, triggering attested CI and possibly CD.
442→- **Fix cycle**: a mission cycle tagged `fix` on the affected milestone(s) after CI red at the gate. Same branch, same PR.
443→- **Rework window**: the span from a blocking signal to its resolution on one feature.
444→- **First-pass active time**: active time outside any rework window.
445→- **Mission overhead**: orchestrator time attributable to no feature; reported separately.
446→- **Waste**: elapsed time that is not first-pass active time, split by cause.
