## config/observatory.example.toml
# droid-observatory configuration (example). Copy to ~/.droid-observatory/config.toml.
# Every value has a default and a reason (ai/RULES.md rule 4). Secrets never live here:
# they come from the OS keychain or the environment (see .env.example).
#
# Status: contract for the mission to implement. Keys may be added by decision file;
# none are read by any code yet.

[mission]
# Default models per role, mirrored in .factory/settings.json and the mission command
# (ai/RULES.md rule 19; docs/decisions/D-006). A change is a decision file.
orchestrator_model = "claude-fable-5.1"
worker_model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
validator_model = "claude-opus-5-5"
# Branch the mission integrates into (PRD §2). "<name>" is the mission name.
branch_pattern = "mission/<name>"

[ingest]
# Where Droid stores session transcripts. Read-only. Raw lines are never copied (PRD §11.2).
factory_sessions_dir = "~/.factory/sessions"
# Attach is the primary live mode (PRD §11.1, D-008): watch the sessions directory with a
# filesystem notifier and attach to every new session JSONL automatically. Off means attach
# only to files picked by hand.
watch_sessions_dir = true
# How often the attach/replay tailer re-reads a growing JSONL file, and the poll that backs
# the notifier when it coalesces or misses an event. 500 ms keeps "live within 1 s"
# (PRD FR-B6, M1 acceptance) with headroom and negligible IO.
jsonl_poll_ms = 500

[github]
# Poll interval for PR, checks and rulesets on the gate. 30 s stays well under GitHub's
# unauthenticated-equivalent budget for a single-user app and is fast enough for a human watching a gate.
poll_interval_s = 30
# App-level override of the merge policy read from branch protection/rulesets (PRD FR-G4).
# "auto" = read from GitHub; "human" = always require the Merge button; "policy" = never show it.
merge_policy = "auto"

[intervention]
# A feature with no active time for this long raises the stall flag (PRD FR-H5).
# 20 minutes matches the troubleshooting examples in Factory's mission docs.
stall_threshold_min = 20

[metrics]
# Price table used for cost when the stream does not expose credits (PRD §10.5).
# Dated file so every cost names the prices it used.
price_table = "config/prices/2026-10-22.toml"
# Mission overhead apportionment: "separate" (default, PRD §10.3) or "equal".
overhead_apportionment = "separate"
# Optional budget in the price table's currency; 0 disables the budget meter (PRD FR-M6).
budget = 0.0

[telemetry]
# OTLP export of the app's own traces/metrics and of lane-9 mission metrics to Grafana Cloud
# (docs/decisions/D-004, contract in D-010). Off by default: the observatory must work fully
# offline. Also stays off, with a visible UI state, when the keychain item below is missing.
enabled = false
# Protocol Grafana Cloud's OTLP gateway accepts.
protocol = "http/protobuf"
# The owner's stack gateway (D-010). Not a secret. Signals go to /v1/metrics, /v1/traces, /v1/logs.
endpoint = "https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp"
# The Authorization header value ("Authorization=Basic ...") is read at runtime from the macOS
# keychain item with this service name and the current user as account. It is never written
# to config, the store or logs. No environment fallback in the app (CI uses B-002's secret).
keychain_service = "droid-observatory/otlp-headers"
service_name = "droid-observatory"
# Resource attributes are fixed by D-010: service.name (above) and service.version (crate
# version, added by the app). No other resource attribute is sent.
# Metric export cadence. 15 s is Grafana Cloud's default scrape-equivalent and keeps
# the lane-9 budget meter near-live without flooding the gateway.
metric_export_interval_s = 15
# Attributes a metric may carry (D-010). Anything else is a bug: never session id, event id,
# feature id or free text.
metric_labels_allowed = ["mission", "milestone", "role", "model", "cause"]
# Active series the app may add on the stack (D-010). The spec states the computed number
# for the metric set below (BACKLOG B-017); the exporter refuses to start above it.
max_series = 200
# Lane-9 series to export (names are the contract; D-010). Counters and histograms only.
# Former per-attribute splits are now in the name (tokens by class, cost in USD).
mission_metrics = [
  "observatory.mission.cycle_seconds",
  "observatory.feature.cycle_seconds",
  "observatory.waste_seconds",
  "observatory.rework_windows",
  "observatory.fix_loops",
  "observatory.tokens.input",
  "observatory.tokens.output",
  "observatory.tokens.cache_read",
  "observatory.tokens.cache_write",
  "observatory.cost_usd",
  "observatory.unknown_events",
]

## deny.toml
# cargo-deny configuration. Checked on every mission-branch push and on the gate PR.
# Policy source: ai/RULES.md rule 6 (advisories and licences).

[graph]
all-features = true

[advisories]
version = 2
yanked = "deny"
ignore = []

[licenses]
version = 2
# Apache-2.0 (this repository's licence) plus the permissive set the Rust ecosystem
# and Tauri depend on. Anything else fails the build until a decision file allows it.
allow = [
  "Apache-2.0",
  "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
  "MIT",
  "BSD-2-Clause",
  "BSD-3-Clause",
  "ISC",
  "Zlib",
  "Unicode-3.0",
  "Unicode-DFS-2016",
  "CC0-1.0",
  "MPL-2.0",
  "OpenSSL",
]
confidence-threshold = 0.9

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
wildcards = "deny"
highlight = "all"
deny = []

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
allow-registry = ["https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"]

## Makefile
# droid-observatory — single source of commands.
# README, AGENTS.md, .githooks and .github/workflows all call these targets,
# so a command documented is a command CI runs (ai/RULES.md rule 5).
#
# Rust targets are no-ops until the walking skeleton lands a Cargo.toml;
# they activate automatically, nothing here needs to change.

SHELL := /bin/sh
.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

HAS_CARGO := $(wildcard Cargo.toml)
HAS_TAURI := $(wildcard apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json)
HAS_FIXTURES := $(wildcard fixtures/streams/*.jsonl)

# Thresholds (ai/RULES.md rule 4: every number has a home and a reason).
# MAX_FILE_KB: source files over this are a review smell; captured stream fixtures are exempt.
MAX_FILE_KB ?= 200

.PHONY: help doctor hooks check check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size \
        check-todos check-decisions-index decisions-index check-secrets \
        fmt fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures build app-dev app-build clean

help: ## List targets
	@grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "}{printf "  %-24s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

doctor: ## Check local tools and print install hints
	@sh scripts/doctor.sh

hooks: ## Install git hooks (one-time after clone)
	@git config core.hooksPath .githooks && echo "hooks: core.hooksPath=.githooks"

# --- Light checks: run on every mission-branch push, must stay under 3 minutes warm ---

check: check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size check-todos check-decisions-index check-secrets fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures ## All light checks (= mission-branch CI)

check-docs: ## Lint markdown
	@markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"

check-links: ## Check links in markdown (needs network)
	@lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress "**/*.md"

check-workflows: ## Lint GitHub workflows
	@actionlint

check-file-size: ## Fail on tracked files larger than MAX_FILE_KB
	@MAX_FILE_KB=$(MAX_FILE_KB) sh scripts/check-file-size.sh

check-todos: ## Debt markers must reference an issue (#123) or a backlog item (B-123)
	@sh scripts/check-todos.sh

decisions-index: ## Regenerate docs/decisions/README.md
	@sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh > docs/decisions/README.md

check-decisions-index: ## Fail if the decisions index is stale
	@sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh | diff -u docs/decisions/README.md - \
	  || { echo "decisions index stale: run 'make decisions-index'"; exit 1; }

check-secrets: ## Scan the repository for committed secrets
	@gitleaks git --no-banner --redact .

# --- Rust (active once Cargo.toml exists) ---

fmt: ## Format Rust code
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo fmt --all
else
	@echo "fmt: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

fmt-check: ## Check Rust formatting
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo fmt --all -- --check
else
	@echo "fmt-check: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

lint: ## Clippy with warnings denied
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity
else
	@echo "lint: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

test: ## Run the test suite
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo test --workspace --all-features
else
	@echo "test: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

deny: ## cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans, sources
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo deny check
else
	@echo "deny: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

replay-fixtures: ## Replay every captured stream fixture through observatory-cli
ifneq (,$(HAS_FIXTURES))
	@for f in fixtures/streams/*.jsonl; do \
	  echo "replay $$f"; cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay "$$f" >/dev/null || exit 1; \
	done
else
	@echo "replay-fixtures: no fixtures/streams/*.jsonl yet, skipped"
endif

build: ## Build all crates (release)
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo build --workspace --release
else
	@echo "build: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"
endif

app-dev: ## Open the Tauri dev window
ifneq (,$(HAS_TAURI))
	@cargo tauri dev
else
	@echo "app-dev: no Tauri app yet, skipped"
endif

app-build: ## Build the Tauri desktop bundle (macOS)
ifneq (,$(HAS_TAURI))
	@cargo tauri build
else
	@echo "app-build: no Tauri app yet, skipped"
endif

clean: ## Remove build output
	@rm -rf target dist

## .github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
# Light checks on mission branches (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 11).
# Target: under three minutes warm. Independent jobs run in parallel; the
# aggregate job `mission-checks` is the single name other tooling depends on.
#
# Rust jobs activate automatically once Cargo.toml exists (walking skeleton).

name: mission-branch

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: mission-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  docs:
    name: docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: markdownlint
        uses: DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2-action@21c1be1b93ad9ed58fa840aacc3f279cde2a72ff # v24.2.0
        with:
          globs: "**/*.md"
      - name: decisions index is current
        run: make check-decisions-index
      - name: file size
        run: make check-file-size
      - name: debt markers reference an issue or backlog item
        run: make check-todos

  links:
    name: links
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@e7477775783ea5526144ba13e8db5eec57747ce8 # v2.9.0
        with:
          args: --config lychee.toml --no-progress "**/*.md"
          fail: true

  workflows:
    name: workflows
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: actionlint
        uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
        with:
          args: -color

  secrets:
    name: secrets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@e0c47f4f8be36e29cdc102c57e68cb5cbf0e8d1e # v3.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  rust:
    name: rust
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable; version from rust-toolchain.toml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - name: fmt
        run: make fmt-check
      - name: clippy
        run: make lint
      - name: test
        run: make test
      - name: replay fixtures
        if: needs.detect.outputs.has_fixtures == 'true'
        run: make replay-fixtures

  deny:
    name: deny
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@3c6349835b2b7b196a839186cb8b78e02f7b5f25 # v2.1.1
        with:
          command: check
          arguments: --all-features

  mission-checks:
    name: mission-checks
    needs: [detect, docs, links, workflows, secrets, rust, deny]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - name: aggregate
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: |
          echo "$RESULTS"
          if echo "$RESULTS" | grep -Eq '"result": *"(failure|cancelled)"'; then
            echo "a required job failed"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "all mission-branch checks passed or were not applicable"

## Concurrency and cost

Measured surfaces (RSS and CPU from ps, build times from cargo output):

| Surface | Startup | Steady state | Build burst | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trunk serve` (dev wasm, cold) | 55.9 s to first HTTP 200 | 35 MB RSS, 0.1 %CPU | up to 7 rustc at 40-99 %CPU each, largest rustc 727 MB RSS | medium during build, low idle |
| `trunk serve` incremental rebuild | 1.5-2.1 s | same | 1-2 rustc | low |
| agent-browser session (Chrome, headless) | 1.25-1.44 s | 1.34-1.54 GB summed RSS (11-12 procs), 0-1 %CPU idle | 40 %CPU browser + 25 %CPU GPU helper for ~2 s at launch | medium (memory), low (CPU) |
| `cargo tauri dev` (native, warm wasm) | 37.7 s to app process (31.2 s cargo build) | app 130 MB RSS, 0.0 %CPU; trunk child 35 MB | native rustc burst, serialized after trunk's build | medium during build, low idle |
| `cargo test` (core-deps scratch, warm) | 2.6 s | - | - | low when warm |
| `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` (core-deps, separate `llvm-cov-target` dir) | 44.3 s | - | peak 7 rustc, 1.27 GB summed rustc RSS, sum 396 %CPU; load 1-min went 3.3 -> 14.6 | high |

Lock behaviour observed:

- trunk rebuild concurrent with a native `cargo build` in another crate: both logged
  `Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache`, trunk additionally logged
  `Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`. They serialize; neither failed.
- `cargo llvm-cov` builds under `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/llvm-cov-target`, so it did not block on the
  build-directory lock held by trunk (0 `Blocking` lines in its log) and only shares the brief
  package-cache lock. It does compete for CPU: the load average hit 14.6 on 10 cores.
- Running `cargo tauri dev` already serializes internally: trunk's wasm build takes the lock first,
  then `cargo run` for the native crate.

70 % headroom rule (use at most 7 cores and 44.8 GB; baseline load 3-6 and about 60 % memory
free per `memory_pressure`, i.e. about 38 GB usable):

- (a) Concurrent agent-browser validator subagents against one trunk serve: **3**. Each session is
  about 1.5 GB RSS upper bound and near-zero idle CPU, so memory allows more, but each validator
  also runs an LLM-driven CLI loop and the page is a single shared dev server with a live-reload
  websocket; three keeps total browser memory under 5 GB and leaves CPU for one build. Use
  `--session <name>` per validator; sessions are isolated (verified above). Do not exceed 5.
- (b) `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexisting: **yes, but run one trunk only**. `cargo tauri
  dev` starts its own `trunk serve` on 3141 via `beforeDevCommand`; a separately started trunk on
  3141 would make the second one fail to bind. Either run only `cargo tauri dev` (its trunk serves
  the browser validators too, verified: `curl` on 3141 answered while the Tauri window was up) or
  point the standalone trunk at a scratch port 3142-3149. Compiles serialize on the shared target
  lock; expect the native build (31 s warm deps) to wait for any in-flight wasm build.
- (c) `cargo test`, `cargo llvm-cov`, `trunk serve` at the same time: **technically possible,
  recommend serializing llvm-cov**. `cargo test` and trunk share the build-directory lock and
  serialize automatically (safe, just slower). `cargo llvm-cov` uses its own target dir, so it runs
  truly in parallel and pushed the 1-min load from 3.3 to 14.6 on 10 cores, above the 7-core
  budget. Run llvm-cov alone (or only with idle servers), and let `cargo test` and trunk rebuilds
  serialize on the lock.

Memory check: at the peak of the concurrent test (7 rustc, 1.27 GB) plus two Chrome sessions
(about 2.9 GB) plus the Tauri app (130 MB), `memory_pressure` still reported 60 % free. Memory is
not the constraint on this machine; CPU and the shared target lock are.

- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/dct/.cargo/shared_rust_target` comes from the shell environment, not
  from `~/.cargo/config.toml`. All cargo-driven builds (trunk, tauri, test) share one build
  directory lock and log `Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory` when they collide.
  `cargo llvm-cov` is the exception (own `llvm-cov-target` subdir).
- `~/.cargo/config.toml` sets `[profile.dev] opt-level = 1, debug = 1` globally; the dev wasm
  build is therefore `[optimized + debuginfo]`, not a plain debug build. The mission's own profile
  settings in Cargo.toml will be merged with this.
- sccache is the rustc wrapper; its Rust hit rate during this session was 0.30 % (`Cache hits
  (Rust) 6`, `Cache misses (Rust) 1993`), so it gives no speedup for fresh dependency sets yet.
- Trunk flags: `--open false` (not `--open=false`), `--config ui/Trunk.toml` when the Trunk.toml is
  not in the cwd. Trunk 0.22.0 prints a `starting build` line and `success` when ready; the
  `server listening at` block also lists every `/etc/hosts`-style name (CRC OpenShift entries
  here), which is noise.
- Dev page HTML contains trunk's live-reload script (websocket to `/.well-known/trunk/ws`); a
  validator that reads the raw HTML must look at `<main>`, not the top of `<body>`. `snapshot`
  already does this.
- agent-browser: no first-run download (`agent-browser doctor` found Google Chrome 155 at
  `/Applications` and reported `Headless launch + about:blank in 1.45s`). State lives in
  `~/.agent-browser/` (36 KB). A daemon lingers per session (default idle timeout 1 h); use

  binary (both reparent to PID 1 and keep running, trunk keeps 3141 bound). Kill all three PIDs or
  the process group.
- The debug app binary is `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/<crate-name>` (`src-tauri` here); match the

# D-002: Tauri 2 + Leptos, with an explicit go/no-go at M1

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (provisional until M1)

## Context

Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. The hard part is `observatory-core` (ingest,
mapping, metrics), not the UI. Rich content (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering)
needs a webview.

## Decision

Tauri 2 shell with a Leptos (CSR, Trunk) frontend; core logic in a UI-free crate behind
Tauri commands with serde types shared end to end.

Go/no-go at M1 completion: the board renders the M0 replay (nine lanes, correct card
positions, Details timeline) with at most 3 worker sessions of rework after the first
scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented
command. If either fails, the frontend switches to Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte) from M2,
`observatory-core` unchanged.

## Alternatives

Tauri 2 + Dioxus (same risks, blurs "why Tauri"); Tauri 2 + TypeScript (two languages,
richest UI ecosystem: the fallback); iced and egui (weak for text-heavy Details).

## Consequences

Named risks: less Leptos in Droid training data than React/Svelte; the WASM/Trunk toolchain
inside a mission is a new failure mode. `rust-toolchain.toml` includes
`wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the gate's `bundle` job installs `trunk` and `tauri-cli`.

## /Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/docs/decisions/D-008-attach-primary-live-mode.md
# D-008: Attach is the primary live mode

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

Missions are started from the terminal in practice (`droid exec --mission ...` in a
project's directory). Every session, including the child sessions of workers and
validators, is written as it runs to `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<id>.jsonl`. PRD v0.3
treated hosting (the app spawns `droid exec`) as the live mode and attach as an afterthought,
which made a launch screen a prerequisite for watching anything live (M2) and left the
dogfooding statement ("from M1 onward") without a mechanism.

## Decision

Attach is the primary live mode. The observatory watches `~/.factory/sessions/` with a
filesystem notifier, detects any new session JSONL, tails it as it grows and renders it
within 1 s, named by its `--tag` or session id. Replay is attach at end-of-file: one adapter
(`jsonl_watch` + `jsonl_tail`), one code path. Hosting remains as the secondary path and the
only mode with a control channel (pause, message, answer over the JSON-RPC input stream).

Milestones: attach moves into M1 with replay; M1 acceptance adds "start a mission in a
terminal, see its events on the board within 1 s". M2 becomes hosting only. The agent panel
and the `model.changed` / `context.compacted` markers move to M1 because they are read-only
views over the same events. PRD v0.4, §1, §9.7, §11.1, §11.2, §13, §14, §15.

## Alternatives

- Host first (v0.3): every observed mission must be launched from the app; nothing can be
  watched until the launch screen, process management and RPC plumbing exist.
- Attach by explicit file pick only, no watcher: works, but the user has to find the session
  id for each mission and misses child sessions.

## Consequences

- Dogfooding starts the moment M1 lands: M2–M5 of the mission that builds the observatory
  are watched by attaching to its own session files.
- New risk rows: notifier coalescing or missed events (paired with a poll at
  `[ingest].jsonl_poll_ms` and a startup scan of the directory); `--tag` recoverability
  from the session files (confirmed in M0).
- `config/observatory.example.toml` `[ingest]` gains `watch_sessions_dir`.
- The Leptos go/no-go (D-002) is unchanged: it judges the board rendering, not ingest.

# D-004: Grafana Cloud over OTLP as the telemetry backend

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted for the backend and the two kinds of telemetry; attribute list, resource attributes and the `active_agents` gauge superseded by D-010

## Context

The PRD needs two kinds of telemetry: the observatory's own traces and metrics (to debug
the app) and the lane-9 mission series (cycle time, waste, tokens, cost) so they can be
charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. The owner provides a Grafana Cloud stack.

## Decision

- Export via OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to the stack's OTLP gateway. Endpoint and
  `Authorization: Basic base64(instanceId:token)` come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` /
  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` or the keychain entry `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
  Never from the repository.
- Off by default (`[telemetry].enabled = false`); the app must work fully offline.
- App telemetry: `tracing` + `tracing-opentelemetry` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics,
  control; errors as span events (no separate error tracker in v1, see B-003).
- Mission metrics (names are the contract, attributes in parentheses):
  - `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` (mission, status)
  - `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` (mission, milestone, feature)
  - `observatory.waste_seconds` (mission, milestone, feature, role, cause)
  - `observatory.rework_windows` (mission, feature, cause, resolved)
  - `observatory.fix_loops` (mission, milestone)
  - `observatory.tokens` (mission, session, role, model, class)
  - `observatory.cost` (mission, role, model, unit, price_table)
  - `observatory.active_agents` (mission, role)
- Resource attributes: `service.name=droid-observatory`, `deployment.environment`,
  `service.namespace`, `service.version`.
- CI telemetry (workflow durations, test timings) is documented only: B-002.

## Alternatives

Prometheus pull (no stable endpoint from a desktop app); Sentry for errors (second vendor;
revisit if span events prove insufficient); no export (loses the external budget meter).

## Consequences

`config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`, `.env.example`, PRD v0.3 §11.4. GitHub
Actions secret `GRAFANA_OTLP_HEADERS` and variable `GRAFANA_OTLP_ENDPOINT` are reserved
names for B-002.

## /Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory/docs/decisions/D-010-telemetry-contract.md
# D-010: Telemetry contract for the Grafana Cloud stack

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (owner-provided contract; code in the telemetry milestone)

## Context

D-004 chose Grafana Cloud over OTLP and sketched metric names with a wide attribute list
(`feature`, `session`, `class`, `unit`, `price_table`, a gauge for active agents). The owner
has provisioned the stack and set the operating constraints below. Cardinality on Grafana
Cloud is billed per active series, so the attribute set is the contract that matters.

## Decision

- **Transport:** OTLP over HTTP (`http/protobuf`) to
  `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp` (`/v1/metrics`, `/v1/traces`,
  `/v1/logs`). The endpoint is not a secret and lives in `config/observatory.example.toml`.
- **Credential:** the full `Authorization=Basic …` header value is read at runtime from the
  macOS keychain item with service `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` and account = the
  current user. It is never written to config, the store or logs. If the item is missing,
  telemetry stays off and the UI says so (a visible "telemetry: off, no keychain item"
  state, not a silent failure). The environment variable `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is
  for CI only (B-002); the app does not read it.
- **Resource attributes:** `service.name=droid-observatory` and `service.version` (the
  crate version). Nothing else. D-004's `deployment.environment` and `service.namespace`
  are dropped.
- **Metric attributes (labels):** only from the set `mission`, `milestone`, `role`,
  `model`, `cause`. Never a session id, event id, feature id or free text. Anything
  that varied by `class`, `unit` or `status` in D-004 becomes part of the metric name
  (for example `observatory.tokens.input`, `observatory.cost_usd`) or is not exported.
- **Instruments:** counters and histograms only. No per-event gauges;
  `observatory.active_agents` is not exported (it stays an in-app view).
- **Series budget:** the spec states the exact metric set and the number of active series
  the app adds, computed from the label cardinalities, and keeps it **under 200**. The
  arithmetic is the spec's (B-017); the shape it must fit is: one mission exporting at a
  time, up to 6 milestones, 3 roles, up to 4 models, a closed list of waste causes, and a
  histogram costs one series per bucket plus `_sum` and `_count`, so explicit bucket
  boundaries are part of the contract.

## Alternatives

- Keep D-004's attribute list and rely on Grafana's adaptive metrics to aggregate: pays for
  the series first, then hides them; rejected.
- Export per-feature series: `feature` would be the largest cardinality by far and is
  already visible in the app; rejected by the owner.
- Read the header from the environment as a fallback in the app: one more place a secret can
  leak into a shell history or a log; rejected by the owner.

## Consequences

- D-004 stays accepted for the choice of backend and the two kinds of telemetry; its
  attribute list, resource attributes and the gauge are superseded here.
- `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]` carries the endpoint, the keychain
  service name, the allowed label set, the series budget and the revised metric names.
- PRD v0.5 §11.4 states the contract. `.env.example` marks the OTLP variables CI-only.
- B-017: the spec session computes the series count and names the histogram buckets.

## .github/workflows/gate.yml
# The gate: the mission's single pull request into main (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 12).
# Everything from mission-branch.yml plus SAST, filesystem scan, workflow policy,
# SBOM, the macOS Tauri bundle (bundle.yml), build provenance and cosign signatures.
# Semgrep and Trivy results are uploaded as SARIF to GitHub code scanning so
# findings appear on the PR and in the Security tab (BACKLOG B-013).
# It never deploys.
#
# `gate` is the aggregate job and the only required status check in the main
# ruleset (docs/decisions/D-003). Add jobs by appending them to its `needs`.

name: gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: gate-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
      has_tauri: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_tauri }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if [ -f apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json ]; then echo "has_tauri=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_tauri=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  light:
    name: light
    uses: ./.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read

  sast:
    name: sast
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    container:
      image: semgrep/semgrep:1.182.0
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: semgrep
        run: semgrep scan --config p/default --config p/rust --config p/secrets --config p/github-actions --error --metrics=off --sarif --output semgrep.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: semgrep-results
          path: semgrep.sarif

  # Separate job: the codeql-action needs the runner's Node, which the semgrep
  # container does not provide.
  sast-upload:
    name: sast-upload
    needs: sast
    if: always() && needs.sast.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: semgrep-results
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        with:
          sarif_file: semgrep.sarif

    steps:

          scan-ref: .
          scanners: vuln,misconfig,secret
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          exit-code: "1"
          ignore-unfixed: true
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()

          path: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        if: always()
        with:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@c3e106d5f8f4253a6de5110efb41a080f83db294 # v12

## .github/workflows/bundle.yml
# Reusable: the macOS Tauri bundle with build provenance and a keyless cosign
# signature. Called by gate.yml (every PR into main) and release.yml (tags), so
# the artifact a release ships is built by the same steps the gate checked.
# Callers decide whether to run it (they probe for the Tauri config first).

name: bundle

on:
  workflow_call:
    outputs:
      artifact:
        description: Name of the uploaded bundle artifact
        value: ${{ jobs.bundle.outputs.artifact }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  bundle:
    name: bundle
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    outputs:
      artifact: bundle-macos
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable; version from rust-toolchain.toml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@a4d3f3f761dcd95cce1b72cb61cb6d1963438177 # v2.87.30
        with:
          tool: trunk,tauri-cli
      - name: build bundle
        run: make app-build
      - name: attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: |
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - name: cosign sign (keyless)
        run: |
          for f in target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg; do
            cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle "$f.sigstore.json" "$f"
          done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-macos
          path: |
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.sigstore.json

## .github/workflows/release.yml
# Release: a tag v* pushed to a commit that is on main (docs/decisions/D-009).
# Builds the bundle with the same reusable workflow the gate used, then creates
# the GitHub release with notes generated from the merged PR's labels
# (.github/release.yml). Nothing here deploys anywhere else.

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    outputs:
      has_tauri: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_tauri }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: tag points at a commit on main
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main; then
            echo "tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} is not on main; releases come only from main"; exit 1
          fi
      - name: tag is semver
        run: |
          echo "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$' \
            || { echo "tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} is not vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"; exit 1; }
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json ]; then echo "has_tauri=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_tauri=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  bundle:
    name: bundle
    needs: verify
    if: needs.verify.outputs.has_tauri == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/bundle.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write

  release:
    name: release
    needs: [verify, bundle]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.bundle.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.bundle.result == 'success'
        with:
          name: bundle-macos
          path: dist/release
      - name: create release with generated notes
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          files=""
          if [ -d dist/release ]; then files=$(find dist/release -type f | tr '\n' ' '); fi
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --generate-notes --title "$TAG" $files

## docs/runbooks/README.md
# Runbooks

Short recovery procedures for the situations this repository and the mission can get into.
Each one states the symptom, how to confirm it, the fix, and when to stop and involve the
human (ai/RULES.md rule 15). Steps that need the observatory app are marked with the
milestone that delivers them; until then the equivalent CLI command is given.

| Runbook | When |
|---|---|
| [red-gate.md](red-gate.md) | The `gate` check on the mission PR is red |
| [fix-cycle.md](fix-cycle.md) | CI red after the orchestrator finished; reopen the mission on its branch |
| [stalled-mission.md](stalled-mission.md) | No progress on a feature for longer than `stall_threshold_min` |
| [hooks-disabled.md](hooks-disabled.md) | Git or Factory hooks are not running |
| [release.md](release.md) | Cutting a release from `main` |

Conventions: commands are the Makefile targets (rule 5); counts and timings are pasted from
the tool that produced them (rule 7); anything learned goes back into the runbook in the same
PR.

## docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md
# Stalled mission

**Symptom:** a feature shows no active time for longer than
`[intervention].stall_threshold_min` (default 20 minutes, `config/observatory.example.toml`),
or the orchestrator has been waiting on a question nobody saw.

## Confirm

Until M1 (attach): tail the orchestrator session file and look at the last event's timestamp.

```sh
ls -t ~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/*.jsonl | head -1 | xargs tail -n 3
```

From M1 the board shows the stall flag on the card; from M3 the card offers suggested
prompts.

## Causes and actions

| Last event seen | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `question.asked` / `permission.requested` | Waiting on human | Answer in the terminal that runs the mission (M2 hosting: in the app) |
| `subagent.spawned` with no child file growing | Worker died or is blocked on a tool | Check the child session file; if silent, send a message to the orchestrator to retry or skip the task |
| `hook.blocked` repeated | An agent keeps hitting `guard-git.sh` or a git hook | Read `build-log/<day>/<session>.jsonl` for the command; the agent needs the forward-only instruction, not a bypass |
| `integration.conflict` | Two worktrees touched one file (rule 13 violated) | Orchestrator resolves at integration; if it loops, stop and split ownership in the spec |
| Nothing for a long time, process alive | Long tool call (build, tests) | Wait one more threshold; then `mission.paused` and inspect |

## Stop and involve the human when

- The suggested action is to change scope, model or threshold (decision file).
- The stall repeats on the same feature after one retry.

// @input: body <<'ARCH_EOF'
# droid-observatory architecture

Authoritative design for the mission `observatory-v1`. Written for implementation workers (Rust,
Leptos, Tauri, CI) who will not read the PRD. Sources, in precedence order: `planning-notes.md`
(owner decisions after the spec, binding), `SPEC.md` v0.2, `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6,
`docs/decisions/D-*`, the two readiness reports of 2026-10-22, `config/observatory.example.toml`.
Where the sources leave a choice, the choice here is marked `[arch decision]` with its reason.
Paths are relative to the repository root unless absolute. Numbers are pasted from the readiness
reports; none are estimated.

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |
| I6 | Thresholds and intervals come only from `Config` (`config/observatory.example.toml` is the contract); no literal in code. | `clippy.toml`; review |
| I7 | Secrets come only from the keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user) or, for the GitHub token only, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Never in config, store, logs, telemetry, test fixtures. The `tracing` layer redacts (§12). | `secrets` module is the only reader |
| I8 | The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5), human-confirmed, named PR and target, logged as a lane-7 event. The app never merges on its own; `policy-merged` is observed, not performed. | `control::merge` is the only caller of `Forge::merge` |
| I9 | Core modules that the UI compiles to wasm (`model`, `mapping`, `view`, `metrics`, `config`) have no platform dependency; platform modules sit behind Cargo features (§2). | `trunk build` of the UI crate |

## 2. Workspace layout

```text
Cargo.toml                       workspace, resolver = "3", [workspace.package] version, edition = "2024"
Cargo.lock                       committed (S)
crates/observatory-core/         lib, package `observatory-core`
  src/lib.rs
  src/model/        {mod.rs, event.rs, ids.rs, lane.rs, role.rs, kind.rs, usage.rs}
  src/ingest/       {mod.rs, source.rs, jsonl.rs, sidecar.rs, capture.rs, watch.rs (M1, feature `watch`),
                     rpc.rs (M2, feature `rpc`), git.rs (M4), github.rs (M4, feature `github`), forge.rs (M4)}
  src/mapping/      {mod.rs, version.rs, v1/{mod.rs, kinds.rs, roles.rs, ids.rs}}
  src/store/        {mod.rs, schema.rs, migrations/0001_init.sql ... } (feature `store`)
  src/metrics/      {mod.rs, time_state.rs, rework.rs, overhead.rs, derived.rs, cost.rs, export.rs, oracle.rs} (M5)
  src/view/         {mod.rs, board.rs, filter.rs, scrubber.rs, details.rs, agents.rs, library.rs, scrub.rs} (M1)
  src/control/      {mod.rs, action.rs, stall.rs, merge.rs} (M3; merge.rs M4)
  src/config.rs     Config + defaults = the example file
  src/secrets.rs    keychain + env lookup (feature `secrets`)
```

## 4. Ingest (`core::ingest`)

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SourceKind { Jsonl, Rpc, Git, GitHub }

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.
    /// Never blocks longer than one poll interval; never returns an error for "no data".
    fn next_batch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>, IngestError>;
    /// True when every known file has been read to its current end (replay = attach that reached EOF, D-008).
    fn at_eof(&self) -> bool;
}
```

`[arch decision]` `next_batch` + `at_eof` replace SPEC §5.4's `poll`: the name says it pulls, and
`at_eof` is what makes replay and attach one code path (the CLI stops at `at_eof()`, the watcher keeps
calling). `IngestError` (thiserror): `Io { path, source }`, `FileMoved { path }`, `TooLarge { path, mb }`.

### 4.2 JsonlSource (S; sidecar and children M0)

```rust
pub struct JsonlSource { /* files: Vec<TailState { path, session_id, offset: u64, partial: Vec<u8> }>, cfg: IngestConfig */ }
impl JsonlSource {
    pub fn open(root: &Path, cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;   // root = the orchestrator .jsonl
    pub fn add_file(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<SessionId, IngestError>;   // child or newly discovered file
    pub fn read_at(path: &Path, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IngestError>; // used by inspect/Details
}
```

Reading rules: open read-only; read from `offset` in chunks of `tail_chunk_kb`; split on `\n`; an
incomplete trailing fragment stays in `partial` until the newline arrives (a writer may be mid-line);
`byte_offset` is the offset of the first byte of the line, `byte_len` excludes the newline; a line
that is not valid JSON is still a `RawRecord` (mapping yields `Unknown { raw_type: "<unparseable>" }`).
Files over `max_session_file_mb` are indexed and a `TooLarge` warning is surfaced once.

### 4.3 Watcher (M1, feature `watch`)

```rust
pub struct SessionWatcher { /* notify::RecommendedWatcher + poll fallback */ }
impl SessionWatcher {
    pub fn start(cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;  // scans cfg.factory_sessions_dir recursively
    pub fn next_discovered(&mut self) -> Vec<DiscoveredSession>;    // new *.jsonl since last call (notify or poll)
}
pub struct DiscoveredSession { pub path: PathBuf, pub session_id: SessionId, pub parent: Option<SessionId>,
                               pub name: String /* first tag, else session id (FR-L1) */ }
```

Design: `notify` 8.2.0 (FSEvents) for create/modify; a poll every `jsonl_poll_ms` (500) re-stats every
watched file and lists the directory, because FSEvents coalesces and a file created before start would be
missed (PRD §14). Startup scan attaches files modified in the last 24 h as growing [arch decision: a
bound so a directory with hundreds of old sessions does not open them all; older files stay in the
library and open on demand]. At most `max_watched_sessions` (64) files are tailed, newest first; the
UI shows "N sessions not watched". Growth is read by `JsonlSource::next_batch` in one `tail_chunk_kb`
step per poll. Everything runs on one `std::thread` owned by the shell (`backend.rs`), which batches
events toward the UI every `event_batch_ms` (100).

### 4.4 Capture header for live attach

`captures` row per attached directory: `id`, `source_dir`, `droid_version`, `started_at`. No file is
written next to Droid's files.

### 4.5 RpcSource (M2, feature `rpc`)

The shell spawns `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc
<flags from the launch screen> -f <mission file>` with `tokio::process` (stdin piped, stdout piped,
stderr to a log). Every stdout line is appended verbatim to the spool
`~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl` `[arch decision]`: a hosted stream exists nowhere else,
`inspect`/Details need a raw line, and the spool is the raw source for `SourcePtr::Rpc` (it is not a
copy of a Droid file). `RpcSource` is a `JsonlSource` over the spool (same tail code, I3 holds).
Control writes go to stdin as JSON-RPC 2.0 requests:

```rust
pub enum HostControl { Pause, Resume, Message { text: String }, Answer { question_id: String, text: String },
                       Approve { request_id: String }, Deny { request_id: String } }
pub struct RpcRequest { jsonrpc: "2.0", id: u64, method: String, params: serde_json::Value }
pub fn encode(c: &HostControl, id: u64) -> RpcRequest;   // method names are confirmed in M2 from `droid exec --help`
                                                         // and the first hosted capture; recorded in the M2 decision file
```

An acknowledgement is the JSON-RPC response with the same `id`; `pause_request_is_written_as_jsonrpc_and_acknowledged()`
asserts it. The child is in its own process group and is killed on window close
(`child_process_is_reaped_on_window_close()`); the readiness report shows why: killing the parent alone
orphans children (`trunk serve` and the app binary reparented to PID 1 in the Tauri run).

### 4.6 GitSource, GitHubSource and the Forge trait (M4)

```rust
pub trait Forge {
    fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>, ForgeError>;
    fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>, ForgeError>;      // Actions runs + commit statuses, never check-runs
    fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy, ForgeError>; // rulesets + branch protection
    fn reviews(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Review>, ForgeError>;
    fn attestations(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Attestation>, ForgeError>;
    fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged, ForgeError>;
}
pub struct Pr { pub number: u64, pub head_sha: String, pub head: String, pub base: String, pub url: String,
                pub state: PrState /* Open, Merged { by: MergedBy::Human | Policy, at }, Closed */ }
pub struct Check { pub name: String, pub source: CheckSource /* ActionsRun { run_id } | CommitStatus { context } */,
                   pub conclusion: CheckConclusion /* Queued, Running, Passed, Failed, RequiredMissing */, pub url: String }
pub struct MergePolicy { pub requires_human: bool, pub allowed_methods: Vec<MergeMethod>,
                         pub decided_by: RuleAttribution /* Ruleset { id, name } | BranchProtection | ConfigOverride(String) | NoRule */ }
pub enum ForgeError { Forbidden { pr: u64, target: String, missing_permission: &'static str /* "pull_requests:write" */ },
                      RateLimited { reset_at }, Http { status, url }, Other(String) }
```

`GitHubSource` uses the token from `secrets::github_token()` (§12), base `https://api.github.com`,
endpoints: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?head={o}:{branch}&base={target}&state=all`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{target}` and `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{target}/protection` (404 → no protection),
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/attestations/{subject-digest}` (best effort),
`PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge`. The check-runs API is never called (planning note 6). Poll every
`[github].poll_interval_s` (30). HTTP client: `ureq` 3 (blocking, rustls) `[arch decision]`: core has
no tokio (I1); version verified on the day with `make deny`. `GitSource` runs `git` via
`std::process::Command` in the repository: `for-each-ref refs/heads/mission/*`, `worktree list --porcelain`,
`log --first-parent --merges mission/<name>` for integration commits → `IntegrationMerged`; fast-check
runs come from `GET /actions/runs?branch=mission/<name>` → `GateCommandRun/Passed/Failed` attributed to
the milestone whose `wt/<m>` merge commit is the run's head.

Target branch comes from `[github].target_branch` (default `"main"`, §11); the mission branch from
`[mission].branch_pattern`. Merge policy: `[github].merge_policy = "auto"` reads GitHub (`requires_human`
= ruleset/protection requires a PR and no auto-merge is enabled); `"human"` forces the button;
`"policy"` never shows it (`decided_by = ConfigOverride`). Gate badge state machine (`view::gate`):
`Pending` (no PR) → `ChecksRunning` → `ReviewRequested` | `HumanRequired` | `RulesetBlocked` | `CiRed` →
`CiGreen` → `PolicyMerged` | `MergedByHuman`. `PolicyMerged` is set when the poll sees `state = Merged`
with no app merge action in `human_actions` for that PR (`policy_merged_detected_without_human_action()`).

Merge button flow (planning note 7): visible only when `requires_human && all required checks Passed`
(`merge_button_shows_only_when_policy_is_human_and_checks_are_green()`); click → confirmation dialog
naming `PR #n` and `target`; confirm → `control::merge` writes the lane-7 `PrMergedByHuman` intent row
with `state = requested`, calls `Forge::merge`; on `ForgeError::Forbidden` the UI shows exactly
`Merge of PR #<n> into <target> refused: token lacks <missing_permission>. Merge in GitHub; the badge
updates from the next poll.`; no retry, the row becomes `state = refused`, the button stays visible, the
poll continues at the normal interval (no storm). The owner merges; the next poll yields `PolicyMerged`
or `MergedByHuman` depending on the merger login equalling the token owner.

## 5. Mapping (`core::mapping`)

```rust
pub struct MapContext<'a> { pub session: &'a SessionMeta /* id, role, parent, model, mission_id */, pub version: MappingVersion }
pub fn map_record(rec: &RawRecord, ctx: &MapContext) -> Vec<Event>;   // total: ≥ 1 event, never panics
pub fn select_version(droid_version: Option<&str>) -> (MappingVersion, Option<Warning>);
```

Version selection: `0.247.*` → `V1`; any other or `None` → `LATEST` with
`Warning::UnknownDroidVersion { seen, used }` printed once by the CLI and shown once in the UI status bar
(SPEC §5.2). `mapping_version_is_selected_by_droid_version()` reads it from `capture.json`.

`mapping::v1` input shapes (observed in `~/.factory/sessions/…` on 2026-10-22, keys only; M0 confirms
and freezes): line `type` ∈ `session_start`, `message`, `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`,
`compaction_state`. `message` lines: `{id, parentId, seq, timestamp (RFC 3339), message: {role: user|assistant,
content: [ {type: text|thinking|tool_use|tool_result, ...} ], modelId?, apiProvider?, reasoningEffort?}}`.
`tool_use` parts: `{id, name, input}`; `tool_result`: `{tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`. Tool names seen:
`Task`, `Execute`, `Script`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Create`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `LS`, `TodoWrite`, `AskUser`,
`ProposeMission`, `Skill`, `FetchUrl`, `WaitForScript`, `ApplyPatch`.

v1 rules (the frozen table lives in `mapping/v1/kinds.rs` and is reproduced in the M0 decision file):

| Raw shape | EventKind | Lane / role |
|---|---|---|
| `session_start` with no `callingSessionId` | `IntentCreated` (first) | 1, Orchestrator |
| `session_start` with `callingSessionId` | `SubagentSpawned` | 3, child's role |
| user `message`, text, root session, first | `IntentCreated`; later ones `IntentAmended` | 1, Human |
| assistant `tool_use` name `Task` | `TaskAssigned` (+ `FeatureDefined` when the input names a new feature) | 2 |
| assistant `tool_use` name `ProposeMission` | `PlanCreated`; `MilestoneDefined` per milestone in the input | 2 |
| assistant `tool_use` name `AskUser` | `QuestionAsked` | 1 |
| user `tool_result` for an `AskUser` | `IntentAnswered` | 1, Human |
| assistant `tool_use` Execute/Script with `git commit` in the command | `CommitCreated` | 3 |
| assistant `tool_use` Execute/Script with `cargo test`/`make test`/`make check` | `TestsRun`; result `is_error` → `GateCommandFailed` else `GateCommandPassed` when the command is `make check` | 3 / 6 |
| assistant `tool_use` Edit/Create/ApplyPatch | `FileTouched` | 3 |
| `tool_result` with `is_error: true` | `ToolError` (`HookBlocked` when the content names `guard-git.sh`) | 3 |
| assistant message whose `modelId` differs from the previous assistant message of the session | `ModelChanged` | 3 |
| `compaction_state` | `ContextCompacted` | 2 |
| `agent_turn_outcome` in a child session | `TaskDone` (`resultKind`), then `SubagentFinished` at EOF | 3 |
| `todo_state` | `PlanRevised` when todos changed | 2 |
| validator text containing a `## Blocking`/`## Non-blocking` findings block (format fixed in M0 from the capture) | `FindingBlocking` / `FindingNonBlocking` / `ScrutinyPassed`; user-testing `QaScenarioPassed/Failed/Evidence` | 4 / 5 |
| sidecar `tokenUsage` (per session, emitted once at EOF or when it changes) | `UsageReported` with `TokenUsage` | 3 (role's lane) |
| anything else | `Unknown { raw_type: "<type>" or "<type>/<content type>/<tool name>" }` | `Lane::for_role(role)` |

Role resolution (`mapping/v1/roles.rs`), in order: (1) no `callingSessionId` → `Orchestrator`;
(2) the parent's `tool_use` part whose `id == callingToolUseId` has `input.subagent_type` (observed:
`worker`); `worker` → `Worker`, values containing `scrutiny` → `ScrutinyValidator`, `user` + `test` →
`UserTestingValidator` (exact strings fixed in M0); (3) `tags` entry `role:<x>`; (4) else `Unresolved`.
Ids (`mapping/v1/ids.rs`): `mission_id` = root session id; `milestone_id`/`feature_id` from the `Task`

## 6. Store (`core::store`, M0, feature `store`)

`rusqlite = { version = "0.40.2", features = ["bundled"] }`. File `[store].path`
(`~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`), `journal_mode = WAL`, `foreign_keys = ON`. Migrations are
numbered SQL files applied forward only; `schema_version` is the highest applied.

```sql
CREATE TABLE schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE captures (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_dir TEXT NOT NULL, droid_version TEXT,
  header_path TEXT, started_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE mapping_versions (version TEXT PRIMARY KEY, droid_version_range TEXT NOT NULL, frozen_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE missions (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, capture_id INTEGER REFERENCES captures(id),
  branch TEXT, state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('planning','building','validating','at_gate','fixing','complete')),
  started_at TEXT NOT NULL, completed_at TEXT, price_table TEXT);
CREATE TABLE sessions (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, mission_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES missions(id),
  parent_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id), role TEXT NOT NULL, tag TEXT, model TEXT, droid_version TEXT,
  started_at TEXT, ended_at TEXT, size_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, tailed_to INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0);
CREATE TABLE milestones (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, mission_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES missions(id), name TEXT NOT NULL,
  defined_at TEXT, completed_at TEXT, state TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE features (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, milestone_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES milestones(id), name TEXT NOT NULL,
  defined_at TEXT, completed_at TEXT, state TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE events (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, mission_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES missions(id), session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id),
  milestone_id TEXT, feature_id TEXT, lane INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (lane BETWEEN 1 AND 8), kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  raw_type TEXT, mapping_version TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES mapping_versions(version), role TEXT NOT NULL, model TEXT,
  at TEXT NOT NULL, duration_ms INTEGER, source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('jsonl','rpc','git','github','app')),
  path TEXT, byte_offset INTEGER, byte_len INTEGER, sub INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, repo TEXT, sha TEXT, url TEXT, action_id INTEGER);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX events_ptr ON events(path, byte_offset, sub) WHERE path IS NOT NULL;   -- the pointer index
CREATE INDEX events_mission_at ON events(mission_id, at);
CREATE INDEX events_feature ON events(feature_id, at);
CREATE TABLE usage (event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES events(id), input INTEGER NOT NULL, output INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cache_read INTEGER NOT NULL, cache_write INTEGER NOT NULL, credits REAL);
CREATE TABLE rework_windows (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, feature_id TEXT NOT NULL, opened_by TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id),
  closed_by TEXT REFERENCES events(id), cause TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (cause IN ('scrutiny','user_testing','integration','gate')));
CREATE TABLE prs (number INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, mission_id TEXT NOT NULL, head TEXT, base TEXT, head_sha TEXT, state TEXT NOT NULL,
  merged_by TEXT, url TEXT, observed_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE checks (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pr_number INTEGER REFERENCES prs(number), name TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
  conclusion TEXT NOT NULL, url TEXT, observed_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE reviews (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pr_number INTEGER REFERENCES prs(number), state TEXT NOT NULL, url TEXT, observed_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attestations (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pr_number INTEGER REFERENCES prs(number), subject TEXT, verified INTEGER NOT NULL,
  url TEXT, observed_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE human_actions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, mission_id TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, target TEXT, at TEXT NOT NULL,
  state TEXT NOT NULL, payload_ptr TEXT);   -- payload_ptr = event id of the stream line it answered; free text never stored
CREATE TABLE prices (effective TEXT NOT NULL, model TEXT NOT NULL, class TEXT NOT NULL, per_m REAL NOT NULL, source TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (effective, model, class));
```

Never stored: raw line text, tool output, prompts, token values, the `systemPrompt`, header values.
`inspect` and Details read `path, byte_offset, byte_len` and call `JsonlSource::read_at`; if the file is
gone the error names the pointer (`FileMoved`). `Store` API: `open(path) -> Store`, `insert_events(&[Event])`
(idempotent on `id`), `events(scope: EventScope, range) -> Vec<Event>`, `pointer(id) -> SourcePtr`,
`unknown_count(mission) -> u64`, `missions() -> Vec<MissionRow>`.

## 8. Control (`core::control`, M3)

```rust
pub enum HumanAction { Pause, Resume, Message { text_len: u32 }, Answer { question_event: EventId, text_len: u32 },
                       Approve { request_event: EventId }, Deny { request_event: EventId },
                       MarkComplete { feature_id: FeatureId }, MarkSkipped { feature_id: FeatureId, reason_len: u32 } }
pub fn record(action: &HumanAction, mission: &MissionId, at: Timestamp, action_id: u64) -> Event;
   // kind: Pause/Resume → MissionPaused/MissionResumed (lane 2, role Human? no: lane 7 ApprovalGiven? see table)
```

Lane-7 mapping (`each_control_emits_one_lane7_event_with_actor_human()`): every action produces exactly one
event with `lane = Human`, `role = Human`, `source = App { action_id }`: Pause/Resume → `ReviewOutcome`?
No: `[arch decision]` lane 7 has five PRD kinds; controls map as Pause/Resume/Message/MarkComplete/
MarkSkipped → `ApprovalGiven` with `target` in `human_actions.kind` naming the control, Answer →
`QuestionAnswered`, Approve/Deny → `ApprovalGiven`/`ApprovalRequested`-closing `ApprovalGiven` with
`state = denied` in the row, Merge → `PrMergedByHuman`. Reason: the PRD fixes lane-7 kinds and forbids
inventing new ones; the control name lives in the `human_actions` row the pointer references. Text is
never stored (only its length); it is relayed to the host over `HostControl` (M2) and, for attach-only
missions, shown as "copy to the terminal running the mission" (no control channel, D-008).

Stall (`control::stall`): `pub fn evaluate(features: &[FeatureActivity { feature_id, last_active_at, last_kind }],
now, threshold: Duration) -> Vec<StallFlag { feature_id, idle_for, runbook: RunbookPrompt }>`; threshold =
`[intervention].stall_threshold_min` (20). Nothing under threshold is reported (FR-H6,
`no_alert_for_waits_under_threshold()`). `RunbookPrompt` follows `docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md`:

| `last_kind` | Prompt (anchor in `stalled-mission.md`) |
|---|---|
| `QuestionAsked`, `PermissionRequested` | "Waiting on human: answer it" (#waiting-on-human) |
| `SubagentSpawned` with no child growth | "Worker silent: check the child file, retry or skip" (#worker-silent) |
| `HookBlocked` repeated | "Agent hits the write guard: forward-only instruction" (#hook-blocked) |
| `IntegrationConflict` | "Two worktrees touched one file" (#integration-conflict) |
| anything else | "Long tool call: wait one more threshold, then pause and inspect" (#long-tool-call) |

## 9. Metrics (`core::metrics`, M5)

Time states (PRD §10.1): `enum TimeState { Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation,
RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled }`. `pub fn partition(events_of_feature: &[Event], end: Timestamp)
-> Vec<Interval { from, to, state }>`, contiguous and non-overlapping
(`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`). Active intervals `[arch decision]`: each event
with `duration` contributes `[at, at + duration]`; `duration` is set by the mapper as `tool_result.at -
tool_use.at` for tool calls and `assistant.at - previous_line.at` (same session) for model generation.
`ToolError`/`HookBlocked` intervals are `RetryFailure`; an open `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested`/
green-but-unmerged gate with no active interval is `WaitingHuman`; `TaskDone` without a validator start is
`WaitingValidation`; a defined feature blocked by another's active interval is `IdleQueued`, else
`IdleUnscheduled`. The oracle (below) validates these rules.

Rework windows (`metrics::rework`): open/close pairs from PRD §10.2 (`FindingBlocking→ReworkResolved`,
`QaScenarioFailed→QaScenarioPassed` same scenario, `IntegrationConflict→IntegrationConflictResolved`,
`CheckFailed→CheckPassed` same check); overlapping windows on one feature merge; unresolved at mission end
reported with `closed_by = None`. Causes: `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
Overhead (`metrics::overhead`): orchestrator intervals before the first `FeatureDefined`, replanning not
attributable, and compaction recovery; reported as its own line; `[metrics].overhead_apportionment =
"equal"` splits it and labels the output `apportioned`. Derived (`metrics::derived`): cycle (feature,
milestone, mission, per lane), waste by the 8 SPEC §5.6 causes, bottleneck (lane/role with highest
waiting + queued; lane with highest WIP/throughput), fix loops (count of `fix` cycles).

Cost (`metrics::cost`): tokens from `UsageReported` (sidecar `tokenUsage`); credits primary when
`factoryCredits` is present; otherwise `Σ tokens × per_m / 1e6` from `config/prices/<date>.toml`
(`[metrics].price_table`); every `Cost` carries `price_table: String` (the `effective` date)
(`cost_names_the_price_table_date()`). Budget meter: `[metrics].budget` or the launch `budget_usd`.
Model comparison (FR-M7): per role, per model, `cost_per_completed_feature` and
`first_pass_active_s_per_completed_feature`.

Oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv`, owner-produced before M5).
Column contract `[arch decision]` (fixed now so the owner can produce it):

```text
scope,id,name,cycle_s,first_pass_active_s,rework_s,waste_waiting_human_question_s,waste_waiting_human_permission_s,
waste_waiting_merge_s,waste_waiting_validation_s,waste_rework_s,waste_retry_failure_s,waste_idle_queued_s,
waste_idle_unscheduled_s,rework_windows,tokens_input,tokens_output,tokens_cache_read,tokens_cache_write,cost_usd,price_table
```

`scope ∈ {feature, milestone}`; durations integer seconds; tolerance 1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD
(`metrics_match_reference_spreadsheet_within_tolerance()`). `observatory-cli metrics <root.jsonl> --csv`
prints exactly these columns; `--json` prints `MetricsReport`. Export (`metrics::export`): same rows to
CSV (RFC 4180) or JSON at the chosen path.

## 10. Telemetry (M5)

Core `telemetry.rs` is pure: `SeriesPlan::from(cfg: &TelemetryConfig) -> SeriesPlan { worst_case: u32 }`
(buckets + `max_milestone_labels` (8) × 8 causes, 4 rework causes, 3 roles × 4 models; 182 for the
configured defaults, `exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins it, refuse to
start when `worst_case >= max_series`), `Label::parse(name) -> Result<Label, LabelError>` restricted to
`mission|milestone|role|model|cause` (`labels_outside_allowed_set_are_rejected()`), `milestone` beyond
`max_milestone_labels - 1` → `"overflow"`, `model` beyond 4 → `"other"`, and
`parse_header(s: &str) -> Option<(name, value)>` splitting on the first `=` (the keychain string is
`Authorization=Basic …`; sent whole it returned 401, split it returned 200 with `{}`).

Exporter in `src-tauri/src/telemetry.rs` (`[arch decision]`: the OTel SDK pulls tokio-flavoured features;
core stays sync, I1): `opentelemetry` 0.33.1, `opentelemetry_sdk` 0.33.1 (`metrics`),
`opentelemetry-otlp` 0.33.1 (`default-features = false`, `http-proto`, `metrics`, `reqwest-blocking-client`),
`PeriodicReader` every `metric_export_interval_s` (15), endpoint `[telemetry].endpoint` + `/v1/metrics`,
resource `service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version = CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. Instruments: the eleven
names in `[telemetry].mission_metrics`; histograms with the configured buckets; counters otherwise. The
header is fetched from the keychain at start, kept in memory, never logged. Off when
`[telemetry].enabled = false` or the item is missing; the UI status bar says `telemetry: off (config)` or
`telemetry: off, no keychain item droid-observatory/otlp-headers`
(`telemetry_stays_off_without_keychain_item_and_ui_says_so()`). One mission exported at a time; switching
waits `mission_switch_min_interval_min` (30). App traces (`tracing` spans) go to `/v1/traces` with the same
header, same on/off.

# droid-observatory architecture

Authoritative design for the mission `observatory-v1`. Written for implementation workers (Rust,
Leptos, Tauri, CI) who will not read the PRD. Sources, in precedence order: `planning-notes.md`
(owner decisions after the spec, binding), `SPEC.md` v0.2, `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6,
`docs/decisions/D-*`, the two readiness reports of 2026-10-22, `config/observatory.example.toml`.
Where the sources leave a choice, the choice here is marked `[arch decision]` with its reason.
Paths are relative to the repository root unless absolute. Numbers are pasted from the readiness
reports; none are estimated.

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |
| I6 | Thresholds and intervals come only from `Config` (`config/observatory.example.toml` is the contract); no literal in code. | `clippy.toml`; review |
| I7 | Secrets come only from the keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user) or, for the GitHub token only, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Never in config, store, logs, telemetry, test fixtures. The `tracing` layer redacts (§12). | `secrets` module is the only reader |
| I8 | The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5), human-confirmed, named PR and target, logged as a lane-7 event. The app never merges on its own; `policy-merged` is observed, not performed. | `control::merge` is the only caller of `Forge::merge` |
| I9 | Core modules that the UI compiles to wasm (`model`, `mapping`, `view`, `metrics`, `config`) have no platform dependency; platform modules sit behind Cargo features (§2). | `trunk build` of the UI crate |

## 2. Workspace layout

```text
Cargo.toml                       workspace, resolver = "3", [workspace.package] version, edition = "2024"
Cargo.lock                       committed (S)

                    lane9/ (M5), launch/ (M2)}
```

| Milestone | Introduces |

| S | `model` (all types, `EventKind` with every PRD §7 variant declared but only `Unknown` produced), `ingest::{source, jsonl, sidecar (read only `id`), capture}`, `mapping::{version, v1}` returning `Unknown` for every line, `config` (load + defaults), CLI `replay`, app shell with nine empty named lanes, `Trunk.toml`, `tauri.conf.json`, icons, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml` wired |

## 3. Canonical event model (`core::model`)

```rust
// model/ids.rs  — newtypes, serde transparent, Display = inner string
pub struct EventId(pub String);     // "<session_id>:<byte_offset>:<sub>"  [arch decision] deterministic from the pointer,
                                    // no hash dependency; <sub> is the 0-based index when one raw line yields several events
pub struct SessionId(pub String);   // Droid session uuid (file stem)
pub struct MissionId(pub String);   // = SessionId of the root session (no callingSessionId) [arch decision]: the only id
                                    // present before M0 confirms where --tag lives; the display name prefers the tag
pub struct MilestoneId(pub String); // opaque; assigned by mapping::v1::ids (M0), e.g. "m0"
pub struct FeatureId(pub String);   // opaque; assigned by mapping::v1::ids (M0)

```

```rust
// model/event.rs — PRD appendix A plus the two SPEC §5.2 additions (source byte_len, mapping_version)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Event {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub mission_id: MissionId,
    pub milestone_id: Option<MilestoneId>,
    pub feature_id: Option<FeatureId>,
    pub lane: Lane,                      // never Lane::TimeWasteCost (computed lane); debug_assert in constructors
    pub kind: EventKind,
    pub role: Role,
    pub session_id: Option<SessionId>,
    pub model: Option<ModelId>,
    pub at: Timestamp,
    pub duration: Option<std::time::Duration>,   // serde as integer milliseconds `duration_ms`
    pub usage: Option<TokenUsage>,

    pub mapping_version: MappingVersion,

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "source", rename_all = "snake_case")]

    Rpc    { path: PathBuf, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32 }, // host spool file, §4.5 [arch decision]
    Git    { repo: PathBuf, sha: String },

    App    { action_id: u64 },                                   // lane-7 action row id (human_actions.id)

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
```

```rust
// model/lane.rs — nine, PRD §7 order. Lane::ALL is the board order; number() is 1-based.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Lane { Intent, Orchestrator, Workers, Scrutiny, UserTesting, Integration, Human, Outside, TimeWasteCost }

    pub const ALL: [Lane; 9];
    pub fn number(self) -> u8;                // 1..=9
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str;        // "Intent", "Orchestrator", "Workers", "Validators, scrutiny",
                                              // "Validators, user testing", "Integration", "Human", "Outside",
                                              // "Time, Waste, Cost and models"
    pub fn for_role(role: Role) -> Lane;      // Orchestrator→2, Worker→3, ScrutinyValidator→4, UserTestingValidator→5,
                                              // Human→7, External→8, Unresolved→3  (lane of an Unknown event)
}
// model/role.rs
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Role { Orchestrator, Worker, ScrutinyValidator, UserTestingValidator, Human, External,
```
